# ForgeJS Guides & Learning Paths

> Structured backend engineering learning paths covering foundation setup, hands-on modular backend construction, HTTP & validation, data/ORM layers, OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 security, and infrastructure plugins.

- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/guides
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/guides.md

## Featured Hands-On Track

- [Build a Production Modular Backend Step by Step (9 Steps)](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/tutorials/playground-backend.md)

## Documentation Modules

### Part A: Getting Started

- [Introduction](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/introduction.md) — What ForgeJS is, its architectural philosophy, honest comparisons with Express, Fastify, Hono, and NestJS, and verified runtime targets.
- [Installation](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/installation.md) — Runtime prerequisites, package manager commands for pnpm, npm, and Bun, CLI scaffolding, TypeScript settings, and troubleshooting.
- [Quick Start](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/quick-start.md) — Build a schema-validated HTTP API with createHttpApp() and validatedHandler(), then swap seamlessly across Node.js, Bun, and WinterCG Edge.
- [Your First Application](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/first-application.md) — Step-by-step typed backend combining createKernel(), defineModule(), validatedHandler(), security headers, and graceful shutdown.

### Part B: Core Concepts

- [Architecture](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/architecture.md) — Unidirectional 6-layer architecture enforced by 60 automated boundary checks across all 20 @forge-fr/* workspace packages.
- [Application Lifecycle](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/lifecycle.md) — Deterministic 7-stage ApplicationKernel lifecycle with boot-failure rollback, lifecycle events, and reverse-order graceful shutdown.
- [Configuration & Secrets](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/configuration.md) — Typed configuration management via createConfigManager(), prototype-safe key guards, and credential masking with secret() and SecretValue.
- [Dependency Injection](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/dependency-injection.md) — Typed DI tokens, singleton/transient/request scopes, captive-dependency detection, cycle errors, and LIFO async disposal.
- [Encapsulated Modules](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/modules.md) — Define modular boundaries with defineModule(), explicit exports, non-transitive encapsulation, and diamond deduplication.
- [Error Handling](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/error-handling.md) — Structured ForgeError hierarchy, production expose: false sanitization, normalizeError(), and HTTP onError hooks.

### Part C: HTTP & API Development

- [Routing](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/routing.md) — O(1) static route lookup, constrained radix parameters, wildcards, nested groups, autoHead, and RFC 405 Allow generation.
- [Controllers & Handlers](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/controllers.md) — Composition-first route registration factories resolving typed DI services via ctx.container and generated via forge generate controller.
- [Request & Response](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/request-and-response.md) — Compact 13-field ForgeContext, bounded body readers (1 MiB default), RFC 9110 Accept negotiation, streaming, compression, and ETags.
- [Middleware & Hooks](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/middleware.md) — Deterministic tiered middleware (global → module → group → route), double-next() guards, and 7 HTTP lifecycle hooks.
- [Validation](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/validation.md) — Standard Schema v1 validation across params, query, headers, and body with Zod v4 fast path and prototype-pollution sanitization.
- [Response Validation & Serialization](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/serialization.md) — Enforce outgoing response contracts with validatedHandler({ response }) to strip accidental PII before serialization.
- [OpenAPI 3.1 & Swagger UI](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/openapi.md) — Reflect Standard Schema routes into JSON Schema 2020-12 OpenAPI 3.1 documents and mount XSS-escaped Swagger UI with strict CSP.

### Part D: Database & Data Access

- [Database Overview](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/overview.md) — DatabaseAdapter contract, SQLSTATE normalization, credential-redacted URLs, and supported PostgreSQL, Drizzle, and Prisma integrations.
- [PostgreSQL](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/postgresql.md) — Native postgres-js pooling, allowlisted transaction isolation levels, SQLSTATE error mapping, and checksum-verified migrations.
- [Drizzle ORM](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/drizzle.md) — Preserve 100% native Drizzle schema and relational query inference with createDrizzlePostgresPlugin() and normalizeDrizzleError().
- [Prisma ORM](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/prisma.md) — Integrate generated PrismaClient (v5/v6/v7+) with P1xxx/P2xxx error normalization and kernel $disconnect draining.
- [Repository Pattern](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/repository-pattern.md) — Decouple domain services from ORM specifics using typed DI repository tokens and explicit transaction propagation.
- [Database Testing](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/testing.md) — Run deterministic PostgreSQL 16 integration suites via FORGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL in CI and local Docker environments.

### Part E: Authentication & Security

- [Authentication](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/authentication.md) — Cross-runtime OWASP Argon2id hashing, algorithm-pinned JWT/JWKS, SHA-256 hashed sessions and API keys, OAuth 2.0 PKCE/OIDC, and Better Auth.
- [Authorization](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/authorization.md) — Segment-strict RBAC, deny-overrides-allow ABAC policies, anti-IDOR assertOwnership(), and multi-tenant isolation checks.
- [Security Guide (OWASP ASVS 5.0.0)](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/security-guide.md) — Clear separation of built-in HTTP defaults, optional @forge-fr/security middleware, and application/infrastructure security responsibilities.

### Part F: Plugins & Extensions

- [Plugin System](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/plugin-system.md) — SemVer 2.0.0 compatibility engine, topological dependency DAG, conflict detection, and frozen capability-scoped PluginContext.
- [Creating Plugins](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/creating-plugins.md) — Author, validate, and test custom ForgeJS plugins with definePlugin(), Standard Schema config validation, and createPluginTestHarness().
- [Adapter Development](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/adapter-development.md) — Implement custom HTTP runtime, database, cache, queue, or storage adapters and verify them against ForgeJS contract suites.
- [Integrating External Libraries](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/external-libraries.md) — Use optional peerDependencies and duck-typed interfaces (RedisClientLike, PrismaClientLike) to keep core packages dependency-free.

### Part G: Advanced Features

- [Caching & Redis](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/caching.md) — O(1) LRU memory cache, cursor SCAN-based Redis cache, single-flight getOrSet() stampede protection, and tag/prefix invalidation.
- [Queues & Background Jobs](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/queues.md) — Memory, Redis sorted-set (atomic Lua pop), and PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED job queues with retries, idempotency keys, DLQ replay, and graceful worker drain.
- [Events & Hooks](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/events-and-hooks.md) — Typed EventDispatcher (fail-fast, collect, isolate error strategies) and priority HookRegistry pipelines in @forge-fr/core.
- [File Storage & S3](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/storage.md) — Memory, symlink-jailed local disk, and zero-SDK Web Crypto AWS SigV4 S3 object storage with magic-byte upload validation.
- [WebSockets & Server-Sent Events](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/realtime.md) — Cross-runtime app.ws() (RFC 6455 Node, native Bun.serve, Edge) with pre-upgrade auth, CSWSH allowedOrigins, and createSseResponse() streaming.
- [Logging, Metrics, Tracing & Health Checks](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/observability.md) — Structured Pino logging with secret & URL redaction, CRLF neutralization, correlation IDs, OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics, and sanitized /health/live & /health/ready endpoints.

### Part H: Testing & Production

- [Testing](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/testing.md) — In-memory HTTP/WebSocket tests, DI provider overrides, plugin harnesses, and dual-runtime Node.js + Bun verification.
- [Runtime Compatibility](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/runtime-compatibility.md) — Transparent compatibility matrix separating locally verified runtimes (Node.js v22.23.5, Bun 1.4.4) from CI-configured targets.
- [Production Deployment](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/production.md) — Strict ESM builds, NODE_ENV=production hardening, POSIX graceful draining, health probes, and reverse-proxy configuration.
- [Performance & Benchmarks](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/performance.md) — Hot-path HTTP optimizations and verbatim reproducible Node.js v22.23.5 & Bun 1.4.4 benchmark results from benchmarks/RESULTS.md.

### Part I: CLI Reference

- [CLI Reference (@forge-fr/cli)](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/cli/reference.md) — Complete reference for all 10 verified forge CLI commands, flags, templates, expected output, and error codes from packages/cli/src/commands.ts.

### Part K: Community & Contributing

- [Contributing](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/community/contributing.md) — Monorepo workspace layout, strict TypeScript standards, architectural boundary tests, and verification commands for contributors.

# ForgeJS Architecture Specifications, ADRs & Benchmarks

> Architectural overview, 20-package directed acyclic graph, verified benchmarks, and OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 release checklist for ForgeJS v1.0.0-rc.1.

- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/architecture/hub
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/architecture/hub.md

## Core Engineering Specifications

- 7-stage `ApplicationKernel` lifecycle (`config` -> `register` -> `boot` -> `routes` -> `ready` -> `listen` -> `shutdown`).
- Strict layered dependency DAG across 20 `@forge-fr/*` packages with zero circular module dependencies.
- Capability-scoped plugin security model enforcing SemVer compatibility checks and isolated DI token visibility.
- OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 defaults across Argon2id, algorithm-pinned JWTs, CSRF Fetch Metadata, safe fetch SSRF protection, and confined filesystem paths.

## Related Documentation

- [Architecture & Dependency Injection](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/architecture.md)
- [Security Overview & OWASP ASVS 5.0.0](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/security-guide.md)
- [Performance Benchmarks](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/benchmarks.md)
- [Build Modular Backend Tutorial](https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/tutorials/playground-backend.md)

## Verified CLI Commands (`@forge-fr/cli`)

| Command | Usage | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new` | `forge new <name> [--template minimal\|api\|modular] [--runtime node\|bun\|edge]` | Scaffold a strict-ESM TypeScript ForgeJS application with runtime adapter setup. |
| `generate` | `forge generate\|g <module\|controller\|service> <name>` | Generate typed module, controller, or service boilerplate following layered boundaries. |
| `plugin add` | `forge plugin add <plugin>` | Register an official @forge-fr/* plugin into your project configuration safely. |
| `dev` | `forge dev [--watch] [--runtime node\|bun]` | Start the development server on Node.js or Bun with optional file watch mode. |
| `build` | `forge build` | Compile TypeScript sources into production ESM artifacts. |
| `start` | `forge start` | Launch the compiled production application entrypoint. |
| `test` | `forge test` | Run the project test suite via the configured test runner. |
| `doctor` | `forge doctor [--json]` | Inspect runtime versions, TypeScript configuration, ESM mode, and workspace health. |
| `help` | `forge help` | Display CLI usage instructions and available flags. |
| `version` | `forge version` | Print the installed @forge-fr/cli version. |

# Build a Production Modular Backend Step by Step

> Build the full opinionated modular ForgeJS backend step by step — from workspace setup and Kernel DI to auth strategies, OWASP security, caching, magic-byte storage, webhook queues with DLQ replay, SSE/WebSockets, OpenTelemetry, and OpenAPI 3.1.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Steps**: 9 interactive steps
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/tutorials/playground-backend
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/tutorials/playground-backend.md
- **Live Playground**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground

## Step 01: Workspace Setup, ESM TypeScript & HTTP Runtime

*Scaffold the workspace and boot the server natively with @forge-fr/node*

- **Estimated time**: 5 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/cli, @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/http
- **Module files**: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `server.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=source

Every production ForgeJS backend runs on pure ECMAScript Modules (ESM) with strict TypeScript compiler checks enabled from day one.

Instead of wrapping an external framework, your entry file wires createNodeAdapter() directly to createHttpApp() and delegates SIGINT/SIGTERM draining to attachProcessShutdown().

### Key Architectural Highlights

- Pure ESM package configuration ("type": "module") and strict tsconfig rules (strict, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noUncheckedIndexedAccess).
- createNodeAdapter({ trustHostHeader: true }) exposes native Node.js HTTP and WebSocket upgrades with zero third-party server wrappers.
- attachProcessShutdown(app, { exitOnComplete: true }) guarantees queued jobs and open connections drain cleanly on shutdown.

### Implementation Code

**1. Bootstrap CLI (`terminal`)**

```bash
# Scaffold a modular backend workspace
npx @forge-fr/cli@next new task-webhook-api --template modular --runtime node
cd task-webhook-api

# Install ForgeJS domain, security, cache, queue, storage, and OpenAPI packages
npm install @forge-fr/core @forge-fr/http @forge-fr/node @forge-fr/validation \
  @forge-fr/auth @forge-fr/authorization @forge-fr/security \
  @forge-fr/cache @forge-fr/queue @forge-fr/storage \
  @forge-fr/logger @forge-fr/openapi zod @opentelemetry/api
```

**2. Node Runtime Entry (`server.ts`)**

```ts
import { attachProcessShutdown, createNodeAdapter } from '@forge-fr/node';
import { createPlaygroundBackend } from './src/playground-server/app.ts';

const PORT = Number(process.env['PORT'] ?? 3000);
const HOST = '0.0.0.0';

async function startServer(): Promise<void> {
  const backend = createPlaygroundBackend({
    adapter: createNodeAdapter({
      trustHostHeader: true,
    }),
  });

  await backend.start();

  const address = await backend.app.listen({ host: HOST, port: PORT });
  console.log(`ForgeJS backend listening on ${address.url}`);

  attachProcessShutdown(backend.app, {
    exitOnComplete: true,
    onShutdown: async () => {
      await backend.close();
    },
  });
}

void startServer();
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Inspect server.ts in the Backend Source viewer to confirm pure @forge-fr/node booting.
- [ ] Verify graceful shutdown closes both the HTTP listener and background queue worker.

## Step 02: Application Kernel, Typed Tokens & Opinionated Modules

*Organize domain features into isolated DI modules with defineModule()*

- **Estimated time**: 8 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/app.ts`, `src/playground-server/types.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=source

As backends grow, flat route files turn into circular dependency knots. The Playground backend uses ForgeJS opinionated modules: each domain folder owns its module wiring, service factory, and HTTP controller.

Cross-module communication flows exclusively through typed tokens (createToken<T>()) and explicit imports/exports declarations resolved by ApplicationKernel.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- Zero runtime reflection or experimental decorators — createToken<T>() preserves full static TypeScript inference.
- Plugins (createCachePlugin, createQueuePlugin, createStoragePlugin) extend container capabilities safely in topological boot order.
- Global middleware (correlation IDs, OpenTelemetry spans, security headers, rate limiting) wraps all domain controllers uniformly.

### Implementation Code

**app.ts Composition Root (`src/playground-server/app.ts`)**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createCachePlugin } from '@forge-fr/cache';
import { createQueuePlugin } from '@forge-fr/queue';
import { createStoragePlugin } from '@forge-fr/storage';
import { createRateLimitMiddleware, createSecurityHeadersMiddleware } from '@forge-fr/security';
import { authModule } from './auth/auth.module.ts';
import { tasksModule } from './tasks/tasks.module.ts';
import { webhooksModule } from './webhooks/webhooks.module.ts';
import { attachmentsModule } from './attachments/attachments.module.ts';

const app = createHttpApp({
  logger,
  providers: [
    { token: PlaygroundStoreToken, useValue: store },
    { token: ObservabilityServiceToken, useValue: observability },
  ],
  modules: [
    authModule,
    securityModule,
    realtimeModule,
    webhooksModule,
    tasksModule,
    attachmentsModule,
    systemModule,
  ],
  plugins: [
    createCachePlugin({ adapter: cache }),
    createQueuePlugin({ queue, worker, drainTimeoutMs: 2_000 }),
    createStoragePlugin({ adapter: storage }),
  ],
});

app.use(createSecurityHeadersMiddleware({ contentTypeOptions: 'nosniff', frameOptions: 'SAMEORIGIN' }));
app.use(createRateLimitMiddleware({ max: 300, windowMs: 60_000 }));
```

**Feature Module Contract (`src/playground-server/tasks/tasks.module.ts`)**

```ts
import { defineModule } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { CacheTokens } from '@forge-fr/cache';
import { StorageTokens } from '@forge-fr/storage';
import { authModule } from '../auth/auth.module.ts';
import { AuthServiceToken } from '../auth/auth.service.ts';
import { webhooksModule } from '../webhooks/webhooks.module.ts';
import { WebhooksServiceToken } from '../webhooks/webhooks.service.ts';
import { PlaygroundStoreToken } from '../store.ts';
import { TasksServiceToken, createTasksService } from './tasks.service.ts';

export const tasksModule = defineModule({
  name: 'tasks',
  imports: [authModule, webhooksModule],
  providers: [
    {
      token: TasksServiceToken,
      scope: 'singleton',
      useFactory: (resolver) =>
        createTasksService({
          store: resolver.resolve(PlaygroundStoreToken),
          cache: resolver.resolve(CacheTokens.Adapter),
          storage: resolver.resolve(StorageTokens.Adapter),
          auth: resolver.resolve(AuthServiceToken),
          webhooks: resolver.resolve(WebhooksServiceToken),
        }),
    },
  ],
  exports: [TasksServiceToken],
});
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Confirm every domain folder exports an explicit module token and never imports unexported internals.
- [ ] View the DI Module Topology inside Health & OpenAPI after inspecting Backend Source.

## Step 03: Multi-Tenant Store & Deterministic Seed Modeling

*Isolate tenant records and expose deterministic sandbox seed data*

- **Estimated time**: 6 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/types.ts`, `src/playground-server/store.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=tasks

Every record in a multi-tenant SaaS backend carries a required tenantId field from creation. Modeling this explicitly at the type and store boundary guarantees queries and authorization checks never drop tenant scope.

Our Playground store hashes seed passwords with Argon2id and uploads starter attachment bytes during kernel.start() so the API boots ready for immediate verification and one-click resets.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- Strict readonly TypeScript interfaces distinguish internal UserRecord (with passwordHash) from PublicUser.
- Two isolated seed tenants (Acme Corp and Globex Labs) let you prove cross-tenant boundaries immediately.
- In production databases, swap the in-memory store token for @forge-fr/database, @forge-fr/drizzle, or @forge-fr/prisma with zero controller changes.

### Implementation Code

**Domain Entities (`src/playground-server/types.ts`)**

```ts
export type UserRole = 'admin' | 'member';
export type TaskStatus = 'todo' | 'in_progress' | 'done';
export type TaskPriority = 'low' | 'medium' | 'high';

export interface TaskRecord {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly tenantId: string;
  readonly createdBy: string;
  readonly createdByName: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly status: TaskStatus;
  readonly priority: TaskPriority;
  readonly createdAt: string;
  readonly updatedAt: string;
}

export const TENANT_ACME_ID = 'tenant_acme';
export const TENANT_GLOBEX_ID = 'tenant_globex';
export const SAMPLE_CROSS_TENANT_TASK_ID = 'task_globex_01';
```

**Store Token & Seeding (`src/playground-server/store.ts`)**

```ts
import { createToken } from '@forge-fr/core';
import type { PasswordHasher } from '@forge-fr/auth';
import type { StorageAdapter } from '@forge-fr/storage';

export const PlaygroundStoreToken = createToken<PlaygroundStore>('playground:Store');

export class PlaygroundStore {
  private readonly tenants = new Map<string, TenantRecord>();
  private readonly users = new Map<string, UserRecord>();
  private readonly tasks = new Map<string, TaskRecord>();

  async seed(hasher: PasswordHasher, storage: StorageAdapter): Promise<void> {
    this.tenants.clear();
    this.users.clear();
    this.tasks.clear();
    // Hash seed user passwords with real Argon2id and seed sample tenant records
  }
}
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Switch personas between Acme Admin and Globex Admin in the Playground top bar.
- [ ] Confirm task lists stay strictly scoped to the active persona tenant.

## Step 04: Authentication Strategies & RBAC/ABAC Policies

*Combine Argon2id, JWT, hashed sessions, API keys, OAuth2 PKCE, and tenant isolation*

- **Estimated time**: 10 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/auth, @forge-fr/authorization
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/auth/auth.module.ts`, `src/playground-server/auth/auth.service.ts`, `src/playground-server/auth/auth.middleware.ts`, `src/playground-server/auth/auth.controller.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=auth_lab

Production APIs rarely rely on a single auth mechanism. Browser portals use HttpOnly cookies or short-lived Bearer JWTs, CLI tools use scoped API keys, and federated logins rely on OAuth2 PKCE.

@forge-fr/auth handles Argon2id hashing, JWT signing/verification, SHA-256 cookie/API key validation, and PKCE state generation, while @forge-fr/authorization enforces role permissions plus ABAC ownership and tenant isolation.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- Password hashing uses createPasswordHasher() with Argon2id defaults and constant-time comparison.
- Scoped API keys enforce least privilege (e.g., tasks:read without tasks:delete or webhooks:read).
- assertTenantIsolation() and admin-or-owner policies block IDOR and privilege escalation automatically.

### Implementation Code

**Auth & Policy Engine (`src/playground-server/auth/auth.service.ts`)**

```ts
import {
  createJwtService,
  createPasswordHasher,
  createSessionManager,
  createApiKeyService,
  createOAuth2Client,
} from '@forge-fr/auth';
import {
  assertTenantIsolation,
  createAuthorizer,
} from '@forge-fr/authorization';

const passwordHasher = createPasswordHasher();
const jwtService = createJwtService({
  algorithm: 'HS256',
  secret: process.env['JWT_SECRET'] ?? 'dev-secret-change-in-prod',
  issuer: 'forgejs-playground',
  audience: 'forgejs-api',
});

const authorizer = createAuthorizer({
  roles: {
    admin: ['tasks:read', 'tasks:create', 'tasks:update', 'tasks:delete', 'webhooks:manage'],
    member: ['tasks:read', 'tasks:create', 'tasks:update:own', 'tasks:delete:own'],
  },
});

export function assertTaskReadable(identity: AuthIdentity, task: TaskRecord): void {
  assertTenantIsolation(identity.tenantId, task.tenantId);
}
```

**Protected Route Group (`src/playground-server/auth/auth.middleware.ts`)**

```ts
import { createAuthMiddleware, extractBearerToken } from '@forge-fr/auth';
import type { ForgeMiddleware } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { AuthServiceToken } from './auth.service.ts';

export const requireBearerAuth: ForgeMiddleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  const auth = ctx.resolve(AuthServiceToken);
  const middleware = createAuthMiddleware({
    jwtService: auth.jwtService,
    extractToken: (reqCtx) => extractBearerToken(reqCtx.request),
  });
  return middleware(ctx, next);
};
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Mint an HttpOnly session cookie, rotate its refresh token, and call GET /auth/session-me.
- [ ] Create a tasks:read-only API key and confirm read succeeds while unauthorized mutations reject.
- [ ] Generate an OAuth2 PKCE authorize URL and verify state mismatch defense.

## Step 05: Security Middleware & Defense-in-Depth Labs

*Harden endpoints against CSRF, bursts, prototype pollution, SSRF, and path traversal*

- **Estimated time**: 9 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/security
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/security/security.module.ts`, `src/playground-server/security/security.service.ts`, `src/playground-server/security/security.controller.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=security

Security controls must protect both the HTTP edge and application helpers. In this step you compose @forge-fr/security primitives directly into route middleware and domain validators.

Every dangerous sink—JSON parsing, outbound webhook URLs, and file path assembly—runs through defensive allowlist utilities before touching business logic.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- createRateLimitMiddleware() attaches standard RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and Retry-After headers on 429 responses.
- createCsrfMiddleware() validates Fetch Metadata and X-CSRF-Token headers before accepting state-changing cookie requests.
- safeJsonParse() strips __proto__ / constructor keys, assertSafeOutboundUrl() blocks metadata IPs, and resolveConfinedPath() stops ../ traversal.

### Implementation Code

**Rate Limit & CSRF (`src/playground-server/security/security.controller.ts`)**

```ts
import { requireAuth } from '@forge-fr/auth';
import { createCsrfMiddleware, createRateLimitMiddleware } from '@forge-fr/security';
import { validatedOpenApiHandler } from '@forge-fr/openapi';

const demoRateLimit = createRateLimitMiddleware({
  store: security.demoRateLimitStore,
  max: 3,
  windowMs: 15_000,
  keyGenerator: (ctx) => `lab:${requireAuth(ctx).subject}`,
  message: 'Security Lab rate limit exceeded (3 requests per 15s window)',
});

const demoCsrf = createCsrfMiddleware({
  headerName: 'x-csrf-token',
  enforceFetchMetadata: true,
  getExpectedToken: (ctx) => security.getExpectedCsrfToken(requireAuth(ctx)),
});

group.get(
  '/rate-limit-probe',
  validatedOpenApiHandler({}, (ctx) => ctx.json({ allowed: true })),
  { middleware: [requireBearerAuth, demoRateLimit] },
);
```

**Input & Path Guards (`src/playground-server/security/security.service.ts`)**

```ts
import {
  assertSafeOutboundUrl,
  resolveConfinedPath,
  safeJsonParse,
} from '@forge-fr/security';

// 1. Prototype-pollution safe JSON parsing
const sanitized = safeJsonParse('{"role":"member","__proto__":{"isAdmin":true}}');

// 2. SSRF URL inspection (blocks loopback, RFC1918, and 169.254.169.254 metadata)
await assertSafeOutboundUrl(candidateUrl, { allowPrivateIps: false });

// 3. Filesystem path-confinement guard (rejects ../../etc/passwd)
const safeTarget = resolveConfinedPath('/srv/sandbox/uploads', requestedFilename);
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Trigger 4 consecutive rate-limit probes in Security Lab to observe 200 OK followed by 429 + Retry-After.
- [ ] Run the CSRF, IDOR, SSRF, Path Traversal, and __proto__ probes and inspect blocked responses.

## Step 06: Validated Tasks Module & Tag-Invalidated Caching

*Validate HTTP schemas automatically and bust tenant caches via tags*

- **Estimated time**: 8 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/validation, @forge-fr/cache, @forge-fr/openapi
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/tasks/tasks.module.ts`, `src/playground-server/tasks/tasks.service.ts`, `src/playground-server/tasks/tasks.controller.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=tasks

Controllers stay concise when schema parsing, error formatting, and OpenAPI metadata happen together via validatedOpenApiHandler().

Read queries cache results under composite tenant+filter keys tagged with tenant:<id>:tasks. Every create, update, or delete calls invalidateByTag() so stale reads never leak across mutations.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- Standard Schema support lets Zod schemas validate query, params, and JSON body before entering your handler.
- Cache lookup sets X-Cache-Status: MISS on first fetch and HIT on subsequent requests within TTL.
- Every mutation invalidates the tenant cache tag, emits an SSE event, and enqueues matching webhooks.

### Implementation Code

**Tasks Controller (`src/playground-server/tasks/tasks.controller.ts`)**

```ts
import { requireAuth } from '@forge-fr/auth';
import { validatedOpenApiHandler } from '@forge-fr/openapi';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { TasksServiceToken } from './tasks.service.ts';

const CreateTaskSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string().trim().min(3).max(140),
  description: z.string().trim().max(1000).default(''),
  status: z.enum(['todo', 'in_progress', 'done']).default('todo'),
  priority: z.enum(['low', 'medium', 'high']).default('medium'),
});

group.get(
  '/',
  validatedOpenApiHandler({ query: ListTasksQuerySchema }, async (ctx, { query }) => {
    const identity = requireAuth(ctx);
    const result = await ctx.resolve(TasksServiceToken).list(identity, query);
    ctx.setHeader('x-cache-status', result.cache.status);
    ctx.setHeader('x-cache-key', result.cache.key);
    return ctx.json(result);
  }),
);

group.post(
  '/',
  validatedOpenApiHandler({ body: CreateTaskSchema }, async (ctx, { body }) => {
    const identity = requireAuth(ctx);
    const created = await ctx.resolve(TasksServiceToken).create(identity, body);
    return ctx.json(created, { status: 201 });
  }),
);
```

**Tag-Scoped Cache Service (`src/playground-server/tasks/tasks.service.ts`)**

```ts
const tag = `tenant:${identity.tenantId}:tasks`;
const cacheKey = `${tag}:${statusFilter}:${searchQuery}`;

const cached = await cache.get<TaskListPayload>(cacheKey);
if (cached) {
  return { ...cached, cache: { status: 'HIT', key: cacheKey, tag } };
}

const items = store.listTasks(identity.tenantId, filters);
await cache.set(cacheKey, { tasks: items }, { ttlMs: 30_000, tags: [tag] });
return { tasks: items, cache: { status: 'MISS', key: cacheKey, tag } };

// On create / update / delete:
await cache.invalidateByTag(tag);
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Load Tasks twice and watch the cache indicator transition from MISS to HIT in the HTTP Inspector.
- [ ] Create or update a task and confirm cache invalidation immediately returns fresh MISS data.

## Step 07: Attachments Module & Magic-Byte Object Storage

*Verify uploaded binary signatures before storing files per tenant*

- **Estimated time**: 6 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/storage, @forge-fr/http
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/attachments/attachments.module.ts`, `src/playground-server/attachments/attachments.service.ts`, `src/playground-server/attachments/attachments.controller.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=attachments

Trusting client-supplied file extensions or Content-Type headers exposes applications to disguised executables and stored XSS.

@forge-fr/storage inspects actual binary magic bytes during put() alongside size bounds and MIME allowlists, then serves downloads with nosniff and safe Content-Disposition headers.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- createMemoryStorageAdapter({ verifyMagicBytes: true, maxObjectBytes: 512 * 1024 }) blocks spoofed headers at the adapter boundary.
- Multipart parsing is size-bounded via ctx.body.multipart({ maxFiles: 1, maxFileBytes: 512 * 1024 }).
- Downloads emit x-content-type-options: nosniff and private cache headers after asserting tenant ownership.

### Implementation Code

**Storage Adapter Config (`src/playground-server/app.ts`)**

```ts
import { createMemoryStorageAdapter, createStoragePlugin } from '@forge-fr/storage';

const storage = createMemoryStorageAdapter({
  allowedMimeTypes: ['image/png', 'text/plain', 'application/json', 'application/pdf'],
  verifyMagicBytes: true,
  maxObjectBytes: 512 * 1024,
});

// Registered on createHttpApp plugins:
createStoragePlugin({ adapter: storage });
```

**Multipart Upload Handler (`src/playground-server/attachments/attachments.controller.ts`)**

```ts
group.post(
  '/',
  validatedOpenApiHandler({ params: IdParamSchema }, async (ctx, { params }) => {
    const identity = requireAuth(ctx);
    const multipart = await ctx.body.multipart({
      maxFiles: 1,
      maxFileBytes: 512 * 1024,
    });
    const uploaded = multipart.files[0];
    if (!uploaded) {
      throw new ValidationError('Multipart upload requires a file field named "file"');
    }

    const record = await ctx.resolve(AttachmentsServiceToken).upload(identity, {
      taskId: params.id,
      filename: uploaded.name || 'attachment.bin',
      mimeType: uploaded.type || 'application/octet-stream',
      bytes: new Uint8Array(await uploaded.arrayBuffer()),
    });

    return ctx.json({ attachment: record }, { status: 201 });
  }),
);
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Upload a valid 1x1 PNG file in the Attachments tab and inspect its generated ETag and byte size.
- [ ] Upload a spoofed payload (e.g., plain text claiming image/png) and confirm magic-byte rejection.

## Step 08: Webhooks Module, Async Queue Worker & DLQ Replay

*Deliver outbound webhooks asynchronously with retries and dead-letter recovery*

- **Estimated time**: 9 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/queue, @forge-fr/security
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/webhooks/webhooks.module.ts`, `src/playground-server/webhooks/webhooks.service.ts`, `src/playground-server/webhooks/webhooks.controller.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=webhooks

Task mutations should never block HTTP response latency waiting on slow webhook receivers. Instead, the webhooks service enqueues durable jobs processed concurrently by createQueueWorker().

Failed deliveries retry with configurable backoff and land in the Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) after exhausting maxAttempts, ready for manual inspection and replay.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- createQueueWorker() exposes deterministic lifecycle callbacks: onCompleted, onFailed, and onDeadLetter.
- Admin-only endpoint guards + SSRF checks prevent non-admins or unsafe URLs from registering webhooks.
- Dead-letter jobs can be replayed directly from the API with optional healthy-sink override.

### Implementation Code

**Queue & Worker Setup (`src/playground-server/app.ts`)**

```ts
import { createMemoryQueueAdapter, createQueueWorker } from '@forge-fr/queue';

const queue = createMemoryQueueAdapter({
  maxQueueSize: 500,
  defaultMaxAttempts: 2,
  defaultBackoff: { type: 'fixed', delayMs: 60 },
});

const worker = createQueueWorker(
  queue,
  async (job, execCtx) => {
    const payload = job.payload as WebhookJobPayload;
    if (payload.targetUrl === 'sandbox://sink/fail') {
      throw new Error('502 Bad Gateway from failing sink');
    }
    if (payload.targetUrl === 'sandbox://sink/flaky' && execCtx.attempt === 1) {
      throw new Error('503 Service Unavailable on attempt 1');
    }
    return { delivered: true, statusCode: 200 };
  },
  {
    pollIntervalMs: 20,
    concurrency: 4,
    onCompleted: (job) => store.updateDeliveryByJobId(job.id, { status: 'delivered', statusCode: 200 }),
    onFailed: (job, err) => store.updateDeliveryByJobId(job.id, { status: 'retrying', lastError: String(err) }),
    onDeadLetter: (job, err) => store.updateDeliveryByJobId(job.id, { status: 'dlq', lastError: String(err) }),
  },
);
```

**Webhook Registration & Replay (`src/playground-server/webhooks/webhooks.controller.ts`)**

```ts
group.post(
  '/:id/test',
  validatedOpenApiHandler({ params: IdParamSchema }, async (ctx, { params }) => {
    const identity = requireAuth(ctx);
    const result = await ctx.resolve(WebhooksServiceToken).triggerTest(identity, params.id);
    return ctx.json(result, { status: 202 });
  }),
);

group.post(
  '/dlq/:jobId/replay',
  validatedOpenApiHandler(
    { params: JobIdParamSchema, body: ReplayBodySchema },
    async (ctx, { params, body }) => {
      const identity = requireAuth(ctx);
      const replayed = await ctx.resolve(WebhooksServiceToken).replayDeadLetter(
        identity,
        params.jobId,
        Boolean(body?.overrideHealthySink),
      );
      return ctx.json({ replayed });
    },
  ),
);
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Register a failing webhook (sandbox://sink/fail), trigger a test event, and confirm it transitions into the Dead-Letter Queue.
- [ ] Replay the failed DLQ job using the healthy sink override and verify 200 OK delivery.

## Step 09: Realtime SSE/WebSocket, Edge HTTP, Observability & OpenAPI 3.1

*Stream live room events, negotiate content, trace spans, and publish specs*

- **Estimated time**: 10 min
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/logger, @forge-fr/openapi
- **Module files**: `src/playground-server/realtime/realtime.controller.ts`, `src/playground-server/system/observability.ts`, `src/playground-server/system/system.controller.ts`
- **Playground verification tab**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/playground?tab=events

Rounding out the backend, @forge-fr/http handles authenticated app.ws() rooms, Server-Sent Events (SSE), weak ETag conditional caching (304 Not Modified vs 200 OK), and RFC-compliant Accept header negotiation.

Simultaneously, @forge-fr/logger instruments OpenTelemetry HTTP spans alongside Pino logs correlated by x-request-id and x-trace-id, exposes /health/live and /health/ready Kubernetes probes, and @forge-fr/openapi auto-generates live OpenAPI 3.1 JSON.

### Key Architectural Highlights

- app.ws() authenticates handshakes with Bearer or query tokens before joining tenant-isolated rooms.
- createEtagMiddleware({ weak: true }) returns 304 Not Modified on matching If-None-Match and 200 OK once bumped.
- registerHealthRoutes() aggregates dependency checks (/health/ready flips between 200 ok and 503 unhealthy on fault injection).
- registerOpenApiRoutes() introspects every validatedOpenApiHandler route automatically at /openapi.json.

### Implementation Code

**WebSocket & ETag Edge (`src/playground-server/realtime/realtime.controller.ts`)**

```ts
import { createEtagMiddleware, negotiateContentType } from '@forge-fr/http';

const etagMiddleware = createEtagMiddleware({ weak: true });

app.ws('/playground-api/ws', {
  async authenticate(ctx) {
    const token = extractBearerToken(ctx.request) ?? ctx.query['access_token'] ?? null;
    if (!token) return false;
    ctx.state.set('wsActor', await realtime.authorizeWsToken(token));
    return true;
  },
  onOpen(ws, ctx) {
    realtime.joinRoom(ws, ctx.state.get('wsActor') as WsActorMeta);
  },
  onMessage(ws, message) {
    realtime.handleRoomMessage(ws, message);
  },
  onClose(ws) {
    realtime.leaveRoom(ws);
  },
});

group.get(
  '/etag-resource',
  validatedOpenApiHandler({}, (ctx) => ctx.json(realtime.getEtagResource())),
  { middleware: [etagMiddleware] },
);
```

**Health, OTel & OpenAPI (`src/playground-server/app.ts`)**

```ts
import {
  createCorrelationIdMiddleware,
  createOtelHttpMiddleware,
  createRequestLoggingMiddleware,
  registerHealthRoutes,
} from '@forge-fr/logger';
import { registerOpenApiRoutes } from '@forge-fr/openapi';

kernel.health.register('demo_dependency', () =>
  observability.isFaultInjected()
    ? { status: 'unhealthy', message: 'Simulated dependency degradation' }
    : { status: 'ok', details: { mode: 'nominal' } },
);

app.use(createCorrelationIdMiddleware());
app.use(createOtelHttpMiddleware({ instrumentation: observability.instrumentation, exposeTraceIdHeader: true }));
app.use(createRequestLoggingMiddleware({ logger }));

registerHealthRoutes(app, {
  registry: kernel.health,
  livePath: '/playground-api/health/live',
  readyPath: '/playground-api/health/ready',
  exposeDetails: true,
});

registerOpenApiRoutes(app, {
  title: 'ForgeJS Live Playground API',
  version: '1.0.0-rc.1',
  specPath: '/playground-api/openapi.json',
  docsPath: '/playground-api/docs',
});
```

### Verification Checklist

- [ ] Connect the WebSocket client, send a live frame, and test ETag 304 Not Modified vs 200 OK after bumping.
- [ ] Inject a dependency fault in Health & OpenAPI and verify /health/ready flips from 200 ok to 503 unhealthy.
- [ ] Inspect live OpenTelemetry spans, PII-redacted Pino logs, and the generated OpenAPI 3.1 document.

# Introduction

> What ForgeJS is, its architectural philosophy, honest comparisons with Express, Fastify, Hono, and NestJS, and verified runtime targets.

- **Section**: Getting Started
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/introduction
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/introduction.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md

## What is ForgeJS?

ForgeJS is an open-source, pure-ESM, strict-TypeScript backend framework built directly on Web Standards (Request, Response, Headers, ReadableStream, AbortSignal, CompressionStream, and Web Crypto).

Rather than coupling application logic to node:http primitives or requiring runtime reflection decorators, ForgeJS separates domain code from host runtimes across 20 modular @forge-fr/* packages synchronized at v1.0.0-rc.1.

- 16 of 20 packages ship with zero third-party runtime dependencies.
- Verified locally on Node.js v22.23.5 and Bun 1.4.4, with a zero-global WinterCG Edge adapter (@forge-fr/edge).
- 60/60 automated architectural boundary assertions enforce unidirectional layering across the workspace.

## Design philosophy & framework comparison

ForgeJS favors explicit composition over hidden magic: typed tokens (createToken<T>()), encapsulated modules (defineModule()), and capability-scoped plugins (definePlugin()) deliver predictable structure without sacrificing cold-start latency or request throughput.

| Dimension | ForgeJS Approach | Trade-off to Consider |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DI & Modules | Composition-first typed tokens & defineModule() | No reflect-metadata or class decorator magic |
| Runtime Portability | Web Standards core + thin Node/Bun/Edge adapters | Pure ESM only (Node.js >=22.18.0; no legacy CJS) |
| Security Posture | Hardened HTTP defaults + composable OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 suite | App services still own authorization & domain policies |
| Database Strategy | Native PostgreSQL, Drizzle, and Prisma plugins | TypeORM, MikroORM, Sequelize, and Knex are not built-in |

## When not to use ForgeJS

- If your codebase requires CommonJS require() output or Node.js versions older than 22.18.0.
- If you specifically want decorator-driven NestJS class controllers or built-in TypeORM/MikroORM integration.
- If you only need a single-file micro-router with zero lifecycle, DI, or security primitives.

---

# Installation

> Runtime prerequisites, package manager commands for pnpm, npm, and Bun, CLI scaffolding, TypeScript settings, and troubleshooting.

- **Section**: Getting Started
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, @forge-fr/cli
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/installation
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/installation.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md

## Runtime & TypeScript prerequisites

- Node.js >= 22.18.0 (verified locally on v22.23.5) OR Bun >= 1.4.0 (verified locally on 1.4.4).
- Pure ESM package configuration ("type": "module" in package.json).
- TypeScript 5.8+ / 7.x with strict: true and moduleResolution: "NodeNext" or "Bundler".

> **WARNING: v1.0.0-rc.1 Pre-Publication Status**
>
> All 20 @forge-fr/* packages are verified locally via npm pack tarballs and isolated consumer smoke tests. Live publication to registry.npmjs.org under the @next tag awaits maintainer execution of .github/workflows/release.yml.

## Install core packages or scaffold with CLI

Install the HTTP core, a runtime adapter (@forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, or @forge-fr/edge), and Standard Schema validation, or scaffold a complete ESM TypeScript project with @forge-fr/cli.

**pnpm (`terminal`)**

```bash
pnpm add @forge-fr/core @forge-fr/http @forge-fr/node @forge-fr/validation zod

# Scaffold a modular project with @forge-fr/cli
pnpm dlx @forge-fr/cli@next new my-api --template modular --runtime node
```

**npm (`terminal`)**

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/core @forge-fr/http @forge-fr/node @forge-fr/validation zod

# Scaffold a modular project with @forge-fr/cli
npx @forge-fr/cli@next new my-api --template modular --runtime node
```

**bun (`terminal`)**

```bash
bun add @forge-fr/core @forge-fr/http @forge-fr/bun @forge-fr/validation zod

# Scaffold a modular project with @forge-fr/cli
bunx @forge-fr/cli@next new my-api --template modular --runtime bun
```

## Recommended tsconfig.json & environment doctor

Run forge doctor inside your project directory to verify Node.js >=22, optional Bun availability, "type": "module", and strict TypeScript configuration.

**File: `tsconfig.json`**

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```

## Common installation pitfalls

| Symptom | Cause | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ERR_REQUIRE_ESM | Attempting to require() a @forge-fr/* package from CommonJS | Add "type": "module" to package.json and use ES import syntax |
| TS2307 module not found | Relative imports missing .js extension under NodeNext | Import local TypeScript modules with .js specifiers (e.g. ./app.js) |
| doctor FAIL on node-version | Running Node.js 18 or 20 | Upgrade to Node.js >= 22.18.0 or use Bun >= 1.4.0 |

# Quick Start

> Build a schema-validated HTTP API with createHttpApp() and validatedHandler(), then swap seamlessly across Node.js, Bun, and WinterCG Edge.

- **Section**: Getting Started
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/validation, @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, @forge-fr/edge
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/quick-start
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/quick-start.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md

## Create your first validated API

Your routing, validation, middleware, and error-handling code stays 100% identical across runtimes. Only the runtime adapter import changes at the entrypoint.

**Node.js (`src/server.ts`)**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createNodeAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/node';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import { z } from 'zod';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true, runtime: 'node' }));

app.post(
  '/users',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      body: z.object({
        email: z.string().email(),
        role: z.enum(['member', 'admin']).default('member'),
      }),
    },
    (ctx, input) => ctx.json({ created: true, user: input.body }, { status: 201 }),
  ),
);

const server = await app.listen(createNodeAdapter(), { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3000 });
attachProcessShutdown(server);
```

**Bun (`src/server.ts`)**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createBunAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/bun';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import { z } from 'zod';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true, runtime: 'bun' }));

app.post(
  '/users',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      body: z.object({
        email: z.string().email(),
        role: z.enum(['member', 'admin']).default('member'),
      }),
    },
    (ctx, input) => ctx.json({ created: true, user: input.body }, { status: 201 }),
  ),
);

const server = await app.listen(createBunAdapter(), { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3000 });
attachProcessShutdown(server);
```

**WinterCG Edge (`src/worker.ts`)**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createCloudflareWorkerHandler } from '@forge-fr/edge';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import { z } from 'zod';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true, runtime: 'edge' }));

app.post(
  '/users',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      body: z.object({
        email: z.string().email(),
        role: z.enum(['member', 'admin']).default('member'),
      }),
    },
    (ctx, input) => ctx.json({ created: true, user: input.body }, { status: 201 }),
  ),
);

export default createCloudflareWorkerHandler(app);
```

## Test routes without binding a TCP port

Pass your ForgeHttpApp directly to createTestClient(app) from @forge-fr/testing to exercise routing, middleware, body limits, and schema validation in memory.

**File: `tests/health.test.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createTestClient } from '@forge-fr/testing';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true }));

const client = createTestClient(app);
const res = await client.get('/health');
assert.equal(res.status, 200);
assert.deepEqual(await res.json(), { ok: true });
await client.close();
```

# Your First Application

> Step-by-step typed backend combining createKernel(), defineModule(), validatedHandler(), security headers, and graceful shutdown.

- **Section**: Getting Started
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/validation, @forge-fr/security, @forge-fr/node
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/first-application
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/getting-started/first-application.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md

## Complete modular service

This end-to-end service defines a private module state store, exports a typed service token, mounts security headers, validates request and response contracts, and drains gracefully on SIGTERM.

**File: `src/app.ts`**

```ts
import { createKernel, createToken, defineModule } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createNodeAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/node';
import { createSecurityHeadersMiddleware } from '@forge-fr/security';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import { z } from 'zod';

interface ProjectRecord {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  ownerId: string;
}

interface ProjectService {
  create(name: string, ownerId: string): ProjectRecord;
  list(): ProjectRecord[];
}

const ProjectServiceToken = createToken<ProjectService>('ProjectService');

const ProjectsModule = defineModule({
  name: 'projects',
  providers: [
    {
      token: ProjectServiceToken,
      scope: 'singleton',
      useFactory: () => {
        const records: ProjectRecord[] = [];
        return {
          create(name, ownerId) {
            const item = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), name, ownerId };
            records.push(item);
            return item;
          },
          list: () => [...records],
        };
      },
    },
  ],
  exports: [ProjectServiceToken],
});

const kernel = createKernel({ modules: [ProjectsModule] });
await kernel.start();

const app = createHttpApp({ container: kernel.container });
app.use(createSecurityHeadersMiddleware());

app.get('/api/projects', async (ctx) => {
  const projects = await ctx.container!.resolve(ProjectServiceToken);
  return ctx.json({ items: projects.list() });
});

app.post(
  '/api/projects',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      body: z.object({
        name: z.string().min(2).max(80),
        ownerId: z.string().min(1),
      }),
      response: z.object({
        id: z.string().uuid(),
        name: z.string(),
      }),
    },
    async (ctx, input) => {
      const projects = await ctx.container!.resolve(ProjectServiceToken);
      const created = projects.create(input.body.name, input.body.ownerId);
      // ownerId is automatically stripped by the response contract
      return ctx.json({ id: created.id, name: created.name }, { status: 201 });
    },
  ),
);

const server = await app.listen(createNodeAdapter(), { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3000 });
attachProcessShutdown(server, { onShutdown: () => kernel.shutdown() });
```

## Recommended modular folder layout

Running forge new <name> --template modular generates a clean domain-first structure where each feature module owns its tokens, services, and route registration factory.

**File: `directory-tree`**

```bash
src/
├── index.ts                 # Runtime entrypoint (Node/Bun/Edge adapter + shutdown)
├── app.ts                   # createKernel() + createHttpApp() assembly
└── modules/
    └── tasks/
        ├── tasks.module.ts      # defineModule() + private & exported tokens
        ├── tasks.service.ts     # Pure domain logic (zero runtime globals)
        └── tasks.controller.ts  # Route registration + validatedHandler()
```

## Response contract stripping

> **SECURITY: Automatic PII Redaction on Response Schemas**
>
> When validatedHandler() receives a response schema, undeclared fields such as ownerId or internal database columns are stripped before JSON serialization. Schema mismatches fail closed with ResponseValidationError (HTTP 500, expose: false).

---

# Architecture

> Unidirectional 6-layer architecture enforced by 60 automated boundary checks across all 20 @forge-fr/* workspace packages.

- **Section**: Core Concepts
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/router, @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/architecture
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/architecture.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Six unidirectional layers

ForgeJS isolates domain services from host runtimes and third-party drivers. Dependencies always point inward toward Web Standards and @forge-fr/core contracts.

| Layer | Packages | Boundary Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application | User controllers + @forge-fr/http + @forge-fr/validation | Translates HTTP/WS inputs into typed domain calls |
| Domain | User defineModule() services + @forge-fr/authorization | Zero node:* or Bun globals; depends only on DI tokens |
| Infrastructure | database, drizzle, prisma, auth, security, logger, cache, queue, storage | Registers providers via capability-scoped PluginContext |
| Framework Core | @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/router, @forge-fr/http | Zero third-party runtime dependencies; Web Standards only |
| Runtime Adapters | @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, @forge-fr/edge, @forge-fr/testing | Implements HttpRuntimeAdapter contract & graceful drain |

## Automated boundary enforcement

tests/architecture/boundaries.test.ts runs 60 assertions across all 20 packages verifying zero forbidden runtime globals (node:*, Bun, process) in core/router/http/edge packages, strict acyclic package DAGs, and pure-ESM exports.

> **NOTE: Why zero node:* imports in @forge-fr/core matters**
>
> Keeping @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/router, @forge-fr/http, and @forge-fr/validation strictly on Web Standards allows identical domain code and middleware to run on Node.js 22, Bun 1.4, and WinterCG Edge workers without polyfill shims.

---

# Application Lifecycle

> Deterministic 7-stage ApplicationKernel lifecycle with boot-failure rollback, lifecycle events, and reverse-order graceful shutdown.

- **Section**: Core Concepts
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/lifecycle
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/lifecycle.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Seven deterministic stages

| Stage | Kernel State Transition | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| configure | created → configuring → configured | Validate kernel and plugin config schemas via Standard Schema v1 |
| register | configured → registering → registered | Register module and plugin providers into the typed DI container |
| initialize | registered → initializing → initialized | Run module/plugin initialization hooks in topological dependency order |
| start | initialized → starting → started | Open database pools, queue workers, and transport listeners |
| ready | started → ready | Application accepts live traffic and serves /health/ready |
| shutdown | ready → shutting_down → shutdown | Drain in-flight connections and stop plugins in reverse topological order |
| dispose | shutdown → disposing → disposed | Invoke LIFO async provider disposers and release container resources |

## Observing lifecycle transitions & boot-failure rollback

Subscribe to kernel.events.on("lifecycle:stage") or register stage hooks via kernel.hooks.add(). If any plugin fails during initialize or start, ApplicationKernel automatically triggers reverse-order rollback cleanup before rethrowing.

**File: `src/kernel.ts`**

```ts
import { createKernel } from '@forge-fr/core';

const kernel = createKernel();

kernel.events.on('lifecycle:stage', ({ from, to }) => {
  console.info('Kernel transition:', from, '->', to);
});

kernel.hooks.add('ready', async () => {
  console.info('All modules and plugins are ready');
});

await kernel.start();
await kernel.shutdown();
```

---

# Configuration & Secrets

> Typed configuration management via createConfigManager(), prototype-safe key guards, and credential masking with secret() and SecretValue.

- **Section**: Core Concepts
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/configuration
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/configuration.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Typed configuration manager

createConfigManager() layers defaults, explicit runtime values, and optional Standard Schema validation while rejecting __proto__, constructor, and prototype key paths.

**File: `src/config.ts`**

```ts
import { createConfigManager, secret, type SecretValue } from '@forge-fr/core';

interface AppConfig {
  readonly port: number;
  readonly databaseUrl: SecretValue<string>;
}

const config = createConfigManager<AppConfig>({
  defaults: {
    port: 3000,
    databaseUrl: secret('postgres://localhost:5432/dev'),
  },
  values: {
    port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000),
    databaseUrl: secret(process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'postgres://localhost:5432/dev'),
  },
});

const port = config.get<number>('port');
const dbSecret = config.get<SecretValue<string>>('databaseUrl');
// dbSecret.toString() === '[REDACTED]'
// dbSecret.reveal() returns the raw string only at the driver boundary
```

## SecretValue redaction guarantees

- Values wrapped with secret() serialize to REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER ("[REDACTED]") in JSON.stringify(), toString(), valueOf(), and Node/Bun inspect output.
- Call .reveal() explicitly only when passing credentials to a database, JWT, or S3 client.
- redactObject() recursively masks secret keys across nested configuration or telemetry objects.

---

# Dependency Injection

> Typed DI tokens, singleton/transient/request scopes, captive-dependency detection, cycle errors, and LIFO async disposal.

- **Section**: Core Concepts
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/testing
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/dependency-injection
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/dependency-injection.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Tokens, providers, and scopes

- singleton — Instantiated once per root container and disposed in reverse LIFO order on container.dispose().
- transient — Created fresh on every resolve() call.
- request — Created once per child scope (container.createScope()) and disposed automatically at the end of the HTTP request.

**File: `src/di.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createContainer, createToken } from '@forge-fr/core';

const ConfigToken = createToken<{ appName: string }>('app.config');
const RequestIdToken = createToken<string>('request.id');

let seq = 0;
const container = createContainer();

container.register({
  token: ConfigToken,
  scope: 'singleton',
  useValue: { appName: 'forge-orders' },
});

container.register({
  token: RequestIdToken,
  scope: 'request',
  useFactory: () => `req-${++seq}`,
});

const scope = container.createScope();
assert.equal(scope.resolve(RequestIdToken), 'req-1');
assert.equal(scope.resolve(RequestIdToken), 'req-1');
assert.equal(scope.resolve(ConfigToken).appName, 'forge-orders');
await scope.dispose();
await container.dispose();
```

## Captive-dependency & cycle guards

| Error Class | Trigger Condition |
| --- | --- |
| ScopeViolationError | A singleton provider injects a request-scoped provider (captive dependency) |
| CircularDependencyError | Provider A depends on B which depends back on A (includes full token cycle path) |
| ProviderNotFoundError | Resolving a token that was never registered or exported |
| ContainerDisposedError | Calling register() or resolve() after dispose() completed |

---

# Encapsulated Modules

> Define modular boundaries with defineModule(), explicit exports, non-transitive encapsulation, and diamond deduplication.

- **Section**: Core Concepts
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/modules
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/modules.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Private providers vs. explicit exports

Providers registered inside defineModule() are private by default. Downstream modules attempting to resolve an unexported token fail fast with ProviderNotVisibleError. Exports are non-transitive unless explicitly re-exported.

**File: `src/modules/billing.module.ts`**

```ts
import { createKernel, createToken, defineModule } from '@forge-fr/core';

const RepoToken = createToken<{ count(): number }>('BillingRepo');
export const BillingServiceToken = createToken<{ total(): number }>('BillingService');

export const BillingModule = defineModule({
  name: 'billing',
  providers: [
    { token: RepoToken, scope: 'singleton', useValue: { count: () => 12 } },
    {
      token: BillingServiceToken,
      scope: 'singleton',
      inject: [RepoToken] as const,
      useFactory: (repo) => ({ total: () => repo.count() * 100 }),
    },
  ],
  exports: [BillingServiceToken],
});

const kernel = createKernel({ modules: [BillingModule] });
await kernel.start();
const billing = kernel.container.resolve(BillingServiceToken);
console.info('Total cents:', billing.total());
```

## Diamond dependency deduplication & cycle checks

- If Modules B and C both import SharedModule A, createModuleRegistry() instantiates and initializes SharedModule A exactly once.
- Circular module imports throw CircularModuleDependencyError during boot before any providers run.

---

# Error Handling

> Structured ForgeError hierarchy, production expose: false sanitization, normalizeError(), and HTTP onError hooks.

- **Section**: Core Concepts
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/error-handling
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/concepts/error-handling.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Built-in ForgeError subclasses

| Class | HTTP Status | Default expose | Typical Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ValidationError | 400 | true (sanitized issues) | Standard Schema validation failure on params/query/headers/body |
| UnauthorizedError | 401 | true | Missing, expired, or invalid credentials |
| ForbiddenError | 403 | true | Authenticated actor lacks role, policy, ownership, or tenant access |
| NotFoundError | 404 | true | Domain entity or route resource does not exist |
| ConflictError | 409 | true | Unique constraint or state conflict |
| ConfigurationError | 500 (boot) | false | Invalid environment or plugin schema at startup |
| InternalError | 500 | false | Unexpected runtime exception wrapped by normalizeError() |

## Fail-closed production error serialization

Unknown thrown errors are wrapped with normalizeError() into InternalError with expose: false. In production, HTTP responses emit only a generic message, code, and requestId — never stack traces or database URLs.

**File: `src/errors.ts`**

```ts
import { NotFoundError } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';

const app = createHttpApp({ exposeErrorDetails: false });

app.addHook('onError', ({ error, ctx }) => {
  ctx.logger?.error('Request failed', { requestId: ctx.requestId, code: error.code });
});

app.get('/orders/:id', (ctx) => {
  throw new NotFoundError(`Order ${ctx.params.id} not found`);
});
```

# Routing

> O(1) static route lookup, constrained radix parameters, wildcards, nested groups, autoHead, and RFC 405 Allow generation.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/router, @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/routing
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/routing.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Static, parameterized, constrained, and wildcard routes

@forge-fr/router compiles exact static paths into an O(1) method-indexed map checked prior to normalization, while dynamic segments and regex constraints traverse a compact Radix tree.

**File: `src/routes.ts`**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true }));
app.get('/users/:id{\\d+}', (ctx) => ctx.json({ id: ctx.params.id }));
app.get('/files/*path', (ctx) => ctx.json({ path: ctx.params.path }));

app.group('/api/v1', (api) => {
  api.get('/status', (ctx) => ctx.json({ version: 'v1' }));
});
```

## Route groups, autoHead & prototype-key protection

- Nested app.group("/api/v1", (api) => ...) composes prefixes, scoped middleware, and route metadata cleanly.
- Route params use null-prototype objects and reject __proto__, constructor, and prototype parameter keys.
- Automatic HEAD handling (autoHead) and RFC 405 Allow header generation are enabled by default.
- Duplicate or conflicting route definitions throw RouteConflictError at registration time.

---

# Controllers & Handlers

> Composition-first route registration factories resolving typed DI services via ctx.container and generated via forge generate controller.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/cli
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/controllers
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/controllers.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Composition-first controllers

Instead of decorator classes, ForgeJS encourages plain route-registration functions that accept ForgeHttpApp and resolve domain services from the request-scoped ctx.container.

**File: `src/modules/users/users.controller.ts`**

```ts
import type { ForgeHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { NotFoundError } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { UserServiceToken } from './users.module.js';

export function registerUserRoutes(app: ForgeHttpApp): void {
  app.group('/users', (users) => {
    users.get('/:id', async (ctx) => {
      const service = ctx.container!.resolve(UserServiceToken);
      const user = await service.findById(ctx.params.id!);
      if (!user) throw new NotFoundError('User not found');
      return ctx.json(user);
    });
  });
}
```

## Generating controllers with @forge-fr/cli

**File: `terminal`**

```bash
forge generate module users
forge generate controller users
forge generate service users
```

# Request & Response

> Compact 13-field ForgeContext, bounded body readers (1 MiB default), RFC 9110 Accept negotiation, streaming, compression, and ETags.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/request-and-response
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/request-and-response.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Bounded body readers & response helpers

- readBoundedJson, readBoundedText, readBoundedBytes, readBoundedUrlEncoded, and readBoundedMultipart enforce DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES (1 MiB) even when Content-Length is omitted or chunked.
- Oversized payloads abort streaming immediately and return 413 PayloadTooLargeError.
- ctx.json(), ctx.text(), ctx.html(), ctx.bytes(), ctx.empty(), and ctx.redirect() construct fast Web Standard responses.
- ctx.requestId is generated lazily on read or error (or preserved from incoming headers only when trustRequestId: true).

## Web Standards compression & conditional ETag middleware

createCompressionMiddleware() uses native CompressionStream (gzip/deflate) with bounded byte caps, while createEtagMiddleware() computes SHA-256 ETags and serves 304 Not Modified responses.

**File: `src/http.ts`**

```ts
import {
  createCompressionMiddleware,
  createEtagMiddleware,
  createHttpApp,
} from '@forge-fr/http';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.use(createCompressionMiddleware({ thresholdBytes: 64, maxBytes: 1_048_576 }));
app.use(createEtagMiddleware());

app.get('/catalog', (ctx) =>
  ctx.json({ items: ['core', 'http', 'edge'], generatedAt: new Date().toISOString() }),
);
```

---

# Middleware & Hooks

> Deterministic tiered middleware (global → module → group → route), double-next() guards, and 7 HTTP lifecycle hooks.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/middleware
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/middleware.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Tiered ordering & safety guards

- Middleware executes deterministically by tier: global → module → group → route, ordered by numeric priority within each tier.
- Calling next() twice throws ForgeMiddlewareError; mutating headers after commit throws ResponseCommittedError.
- Compiled pipelines are cached directly on each route object (route._pipelineRun) for zero-allocation hot-path dispatch.

## Seven HTTP lifecycle hooks

| Hook | Execution Point | Typical Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| onRequest | Before route matching | Request metrics, custom tracing span start |
| preValidation | After route match, before schema validation | Header normalization or tenant extraction |
| preHandler | After validation, before route handler | Route-level authorization checks |
| preSerialization | After handler returns payload, before JSON stringify | Envelope formatting or field auditing |
| onSend | Before final Response leaves app.fetch() | Appending custom response headers |
| onError | When any middleware or handler throws | Structured error logging with ctx.requestId |
| onResponse | After response is finalized | Latency histograms and access logs |

---

# Validation

> Standard Schema v1 validation across params, query, headers, and body with Zod v4 fast path and prototype-pollution sanitization.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/validation
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/validation
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/validation.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Zod v4, Valibot v1 & Standard Schema v1

@forge-fr/validation supports any @standard-schema/spec v1 schema natively (Zod v4, Valibot v1, ArkType) plus zodAdapter for legacy Zod v3 and customSchema() for bespoke validators. Incoming JSON bodies are scanned to strip __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys automatically.

**File: `src/validated-route.ts`**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import * as v from 'valibot';
import { z } from 'zod';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.post(
  '/projects/:projectId/tasks',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      params: z.object({ projectId: z.string().min(2) }),
      query: v.object({ dryRun: v.optional(v.string()) }),
      body: z.object({ title: z.string().min(3) }),
    },
    (ctx, input) =>
      ctx.json(
        {
          projectId: input.params.projectId,
          dryRun: input.query.dryRun === 'true',
          title: input.body.title,
        },
        { status: 201 },
      ),
  ),
);
```

## Compiled Zod v4 fast path

compileFastValidator() detects synchronous Zod v4 schemas once at route registration and invokes safeParse() directly (2.6x faster than ~standard.validate), falling back automatically to Standard Schema validate() for async refinements, Valibot, or custom validators.

---

# Response Validation & Serialization

> Enforce outgoing response contracts with validatedHandler({ response }) to strip accidental PII before serialization.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/validation, @forge-fr/http
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/serialization
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/serialization.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Fail-closed response schemas

Passing a response schema to validatedHandler() validates and strips outgoing payloads before serialization. Contract violations throw ResponseValidationError (HTTP 500, expose: false) so internal schema defects are logged privately rather than leaked.

**File: `src/response-contract.ts`**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import { z } from 'zod';

const PublicUserSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  displayName: z.string(),
});

const app = createHttpApp();

app.get(
  '/users/:id',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      params: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
      response: PublicUserSchema,
    },
    (_ctx, input) => ({
      id: input.params.id,
      displayName: 'Ada Lovelace',
      // passwordHash is stripped automatically by PublicUserSchema
      passwordHash: '$argon2id$...',
    }),
  ),
);
```

# OpenAPI 3.1 & Swagger UI

> Reflect Standard Schema routes into JSON Schema 2020-12 OpenAPI 3.1 documents and mount XSS-escaped Swagger UI with strict CSP.

- **Section**: HTTP & API Development
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/openapi, @forge-fr/validation
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/openapi
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/http/openapi.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Generating OpenAPI 3.1 specs & hardened Swagger UI

validatedOpenApiHandler(schemas, handler, metadata) attaches typed OpenAPI metadata while enforcing runtime validation. registerOpenApiRoutes(app, { title, version }) serves /openapi.json and an XSS-escaped /docs Swagger UI page with strict Content-Security-Policy headers.

**File: `src/openapi.ts`**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import {
  generateOpenApiDocument,
  registerOpenApiRoutes,
  validatedOpenApiHandler,
} from '@forge-fr/openapi';
import { z } from 'zod';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.get(
  '/items/:id',
  validatedOpenApiHandler(
    {
      params: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
      response: z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string() }),
    },
    (_ctx, input) => ({ id: input.params.id, name: 'Widget' }),
    { operationId: 'getItem', summary: 'Fetch item by ID', tags: ['Items'] },
  ),
);

registerOpenApiRoutes(app, {
  title: 'Forge Store API',
  version: '1.0.0',
});

const spec = generateOpenApiDocument(app, { title: 'Forge Store API', version: '1.0.0' });
```

## Swagger UI security posture

> **SECURITY: XSS Escaping & Production Visibility**
>
> renderSwaggerUiHtml() escapes spec titles and URLs and sets object-src 'none' CSP headers. Consider gating /docs behind authentication or disabling Swagger UI in public internet deployments.
