# Database Overview

> DatabaseAdapter contract, SQLSTATE normalization, credential-redacted URLs, and supported PostgreSQL, Drizzle, and Prisma integrations.

- **Section**: Database & Data Access
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/database, @forge-fr/drizzle, @forge-fr/prisma
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/overview
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/overview.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## Verified official integrations

- @forge-fr/database — Native PostgreSQL driver built on postgres (postgres-js) with pooling, transactions, migrations, and SQLSTATE error mapping.
- @forge-fr/drizzle — First-class Drizzle ORM plugin preserving 100% native PostgresJsDatabase<TSchema> inference.
- @forge-fr/prisma — Prisma ORM plugin supporting Prisma v5/v6/v7+ generated clients with P1xxx/P2xxx error normalization.

> **NOTE: Explicit ORM Scope Disclosure**
>
> TypeORM, MikroORM, Sequelize, and Knex do not have official ForgeJS packages. Teams using other ORMs or SQL dialects can integrate them cleanly via the generic DatabaseAdapter contract and createDatabasePlugin().

## Credential redaction & SQLSTATE normalization

All database adapters sanitize connection strings via redactDatabaseUrl() and map raw driver errors into typed ForgeError subclasses with expose: false by default so SQL statements and credentials never leak.

**File: `src/db/errors.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {
  DatabaseUniqueViolationError,
  normalizeDatabaseError,
  redactDatabaseUrl,
} from '@forge-fr/database';

const safeUrl = redactDatabaseUrl('postgres://admin:top_secret@db.internal:5432/prod');
assert.ok(safeUrl.includes('admin:[REDACTED]@db.internal:5432/prod'));

const normalized = normalizeDatabaseError({
  code: '23505',
  message: 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint',
});
assert.ok(normalized instanceof DatabaseUniqueViolationError);
assert.equal(normalized.expose, false);
```

# PostgreSQL

> Native postgres-js pooling, allowlisted transaction isolation levels, SQLSTATE error mapping, and checksum-verified migrations.

- **Section**: Database & Data Access
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/database
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/postgresql
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/postgresql.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## Registering the PostgreSQL plugin & running transactions

Pass createPostgresPlugin() and its runtime config tuple into createKernel({ plugins }) or call kernel.plugin(createPostgresPlugin(), config). The plugin automatically registers a health probe and closes the pool cleanly on kernel.shutdown().

**File: `src/db/postgres.ts`**

```ts
import { createKernel, secret } from '@forge-fr/core';
import {
  createPostgresPlugin,
  DefaultDatabaseTokens,
  runInTransaction,
} from '@forge-fr/database';

const kernel = createKernel({
  plugins: [
    [
      createPostgresPlugin(),
      {
        url: secret(process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? ''),
        max: 20,
      },
    ],
  ],
});

await kernel.start();
const adapter = kernel.container.resolve(DefaultDatabaseTokens.adapter);

await runInTransaction(
  adapter,
  async (tx) => {
    await tx`INSERT INTO audit_events (event_type) VALUES (${'boot'})`;
  },
  { isolationLevel: 'read committed' },
);
```

## Checksum-verified SQL migrations

createMigrationRunner() tracks applied migrations with SHA-256 checksums, rejecting tampered historical migrations before executing new SQL files.

| Isolation Level (Allowlisted) | SQLSTATE Mapped Errors |
| --- | --- |
| read uncommitted · read committed | 23505 → DatabaseUniqueViolationError (409 internal) |
| repeatable read · serializable | 23503 → DatabaseForeignKeyError · 40001/40P01 → DatabaseSerializationError |

---

# Drizzle ORM

> Preserve 100% native Drizzle schema and relational query inference with createDrizzlePostgresPlugin() and normalizeDrizzleError().

- **Section**: Database & Data Access
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/drizzle, @forge-fr/database
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/drizzle
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/drizzle.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## Zero-loss Drizzle TypeScript inference

Passing your schema generic to createDrizzlePostgresPlugin<typeof schema>() preserves complete Drizzle query builder and relational db.query.* inference with zero wrapper abstractions.

**File: `src/db/drizzle.ts`**

```ts
import { createKernel, secret } from '@forge-fr/core';
import {
  createDrizzlePostgresPlugin,
  DefaultDrizzleTokens,
} from '@forge-fr/drizzle';
import * as schema from './schema.js';

const kernel = createKernel({
  plugins: [
    [
      createDrizzlePostgresPlugin<typeof schema>(),
      {
        url: secret(process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? ''),
        schema,
      },
    ],
  ],
});

await kernel.start();
const db = kernel.container.resolve(DefaultDrizzleTokens.db);
```

## Transactions & error normalization

- The Drizzle adapter implements DatabaseAdapter.transaction() with allowlisted isolation levels and wraps failures through normalizeDrizzleError().
- Shutdown automatically closes the underlying postgres-js pool via LIFO kernel teardown.

# Prisma ORM

> Integrate generated PrismaClient (v5/v6/v7+) with P1xxx/P2xxx error normalization and kernel $disconnect draining.

- **Section**: Database & Data Access
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/prisma, @forge-fr/database
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/prisma
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/prisma.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## Registering PrismaClient with the kernel

@forge-fr/prisma accepts any duck-typed PrismaClientLike instance (supporting Prisma v5, v6, and v7+ driver adapters) without pinning @prisma/client as a hard runtime dependency.

**File: `src/db/prisma.ts`**

```ts
import { createKernel } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createPrismaPlugin, DefaultPrismaTokens } from '@forge-fr/prisma';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';

const kernel = createKernel({
  plugins: [
    [createPrismaPlugin(), { client: new PrismaClient() }],
  ],
});

await kernel.start();
const prisma = kernel.container.resolve(DefaultPrismaTokens.client);
```

## Prisma P1xxx/P2xxx error mapping

| Prisma Error Code | Mapped ForgeJS Database Error |
| --- | --- |
| P2002 | DatabaseUniqueViolationError |
| P2003 | DatabaseForeignKeyError |
| P2034 | DatabaseSerializationError |
| P1001 / P1002 / P1008 | DatabaseConnectionError / DatabaseTimeoutError |

# Repository Pattern

> Decouple domain services from ORM specifics using typed DI repository tokens and explicit transaction propagation.

- **Section**: Database & Data Access
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/database, @forge-fr/testing
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/repository-pattern
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/database/repository-pattern.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## Port interfaces & provider overrides

Define domain repository interfaces behind createToken<T>(), bind PostgreSQL/Drizzle/Prisma implementations inside infrastructure modules, and swap them cleanly in unit tests via overrideProvider().

**File: `src/modules/orders/orders.repository.ts`**

```ts
import { createToken, defineModule } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { DefaultDrizzleTokens } from '@forge-fr/drizzle';

export interface OrderRecord {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly totalCents: number;
}

export interface OrderRepository {
  findById(id: string): Promise<OrderRecord | null>;
}

export const OrderRepositoryToken = createToken<OrderRepository>('OrderRepository');

export const OrderDataModule = defineModule({
  name: 'orders-data',
  providers: [
    {
      token: OrderRepositoryToken,
      scope: 'singleton',
      inject: [DefaultDrizzleTokens.db] as const,
      useFactory: (_db): OrderRepository => ({
        async findById(id) {
          return { id, totalCents: 4200 };
        },
      }),
    },
  ],
  exports: [OrderRepositoryToken],
});
```

When FORGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset locally, suites explicitly report SKIPPED rather than falsely passing.

**File: `terminal`**

```bash
# Run live PostgreSQL 16 integration tests against local Docker

FORGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:forge@127.0.0.1:5432/forge_test npx vitest run
```

# Authentication

> Cross-runtime OWASP Argon2id hashing, algorithm-pinned JWT/JWKS, SHA-256 hashed sessions and API keys, OAuth 2.0 PKCE/OIDC, and Better Auth.

- **Section**: Authentication & Security
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/auth
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/authentication
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/authentication.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## Password hashing, algorithm-pinned JWTs & hashed sessions

- createArgon2PasswordHasher() enforces OWASP Argon2id floors (memoryCost >= 12288 KiB, default 19456, timeCost >= 2, 1024-byte cap) and is verified cross-compatible between @node-rs/argon2 and Bun.password.
- createJwtService() requires an explicit algorithms allowlist, rejects alg: none, and enforces >=32-byte HMAC secrets.
- Session IDs and API keys are stored strictly as SHA-256 hex digests and verified in constant time.

**File: `src/auth.ts`**

```ts
import { secret } from '@forge-fr/core';
import {
  createArgon2PasswordHasher,
  createJwtService,
  createMemorySessionStore,
  createSessionManager,
} from '@forge-fr/auth';

const hasher = createArgon2PasswordHasher();
const hash = await hasher.hash('CorrectHorseBattery99!');
const valid = await hasher.verify('CorrectHorseBattery99!', hash);

const jwt = createJwtService({
  algorithms: ['HS256'],
  secret: secret('super-secret-signing-key-at-least-32-bytes'),
  issuer: 'https://auth.example.com',
  audience: 'forge-api',
});
const token = await jwt.sign({ sub: 'user-1', role: 'editor' }, { expiresIn: '10m' });

const sessions = createSessionManager({
  store: createMemorySessionStore(),
  idleTtlMs: 30 * 60_000,
  absoluteTtlMs: 24 * 60 * 60_000,
});
```

## OAuth 2.0 PKCE / OIDC & Better Auth bridge

@forge-fr/auth includes createOAuthPkceClient() (S256 PKCE + state/nonce validation), createApiKeyService(), and mountBetterAuth() / createBetterAuthBridge() for teams adopting Better Auth.

# Authorization

> Segment-strict RBAC, deny-overrides-allow ABAC policies, anti-IDOR assertOwnership(), and multi-tenant isolation checks.

- **Section**: Authentication & Security
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/authorization
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/authorization
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/authorization.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/data-and-auth.md

## RBAC, ABAC policies & multi-tenant isolation

createAuthorizer() evaluates RBAC roles, explicit deniedPermissions, ABAC policies, and tenant isolation identically in both HTTP middleware and pure domain services via authorizer.forActor(actor). Deny always overrides allow.

**File: `src/authz.ts`**

```ts
import {
  assertOwnership,
  createAuthorizer,
  definePolicy,
} from '@forge-fr/authorization';

const authorizer = createAuthorizer({
  enforceTenantIsolation: true,
  roles: {
    viewer: { permissions: ['invoice:read'] },
    billingAdmin: {
      inherits: ['viewer'],
      permissions: ['invoice:*'],
      deniedPermissions: ['invoice:delete'],
    },
  },
  policies: [
    definePolicy({
      name: 'deny-suspended-actor',
      effect: 'deny',
      actions: ['*'],
      condition: ({ actor }) => actor.attributes?.['suspended'] === true,
    }),
  ],
});

const billing = authorizer.forActor({
  subject: 'u-10',
  tenantId: 'tenant-a',
  roles: ['billingAdmin'],
  permissions: [],
  scopes: [],
});

const decision = await billing.evaluate('invoice:update', { tenantId: 'tenant-a' });
assertOwnership(billing.actor, { ownerId: 'u-10' });
```

# Security Guide (OWASP ASVS 5.0.0)

> Clear separation of built-in HTTP defaults, optional @forge-fr/security middleware, and application/infrastructure security responsibilities.

- **Section**: Authentication & Security
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/security, @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/storage, @forge-fr/logger
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/security-guide
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/security/security-guide.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/security-and-observability.md

## Composable OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 controls

@forge-fr/security ships zero-dependency security middleware and utility guards aligned with OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1/L2 baseline controls.

**File: `src/security.ts`**

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import {
  createCorsMiddleware,
  createCsrfMiddleware,
  createRateLimitMiddleware,
  createSafeFetch,
  createSecurityHeadersMiddleware,
  resolveConfinedPath,
  sanitizeObject,
} from '@forge-fr/security';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.use(createSecurityHeadersMiddleware());
app.use(createCorsMiddleware({ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }));
app.use(createCsrfMiddleware());
app.use(createRateLimitMiddleware({ windowMs: 60_000, max: 120, trustProxy: false }));

// SSRF-hardened outbound fetch (blocks loopback, link-local, RFC1918, cloud metadata)
const safeFetch = createSafeFetch();
const safePath = resolveConfinedPath('/var/app/uploads', '2026/avatar.png');
const clean = sanitizeObject({ name: 'alice' });
```

## Built-in defaults vs. optional vs. application duties

| Layer | Included Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Built-in Framework Defaults | 1 MiB bounded body readers (413), null-prototype params, prototype-pollution stripping, expose: false 5xx sanitization, CRLF log stripping, SecretValue redaction |
| Optional @forge-fr/security & @forge-fr/auth | CSP/HSTS headers, strict CORS, double-submit CSRF, rate limiting, SSRF createSafeFetch(), Argon2id, algorithm-pinned JWT, RBAC/ABAC |
| Application & Infrastructure Duties | Calling assertOwnership() & assertTenantIsolation() on every object fetch, TLS termination, WAF/DDoS, secret rotation, OS/container isolation |

## Limitations & honest boundaries

> **SECURITY: Honest Security Boundary**
>
> No framework automatically makes an application secure. Plugins run in-process (capability scoping prevents accidental coupling, not OS/VM sandboxing). Schema validation proves shape only; services must still enforce ownership and tenant checks.

---

# Plugin System

> SemVer 2.0.0 compatibility engine, topological dependency DAG, conflict detection, and frozen capability-scoped PluginContext.

- **Section**: Plugins & Extensions
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/plugin-system
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/plugin-system.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Declared capabilities & frozen PluginContext

Every ForgeJS plugin explicitly declares the capabilities it requires. During kernel boot, createPluginContext() creates a frozen context object whose methods enforce capability boundaries at runtime.

| Capability | Permitted PluginContext Operation |
| --- | --- |
| di:register | Register private or explicitly exported providers into the container |
| di:resolve | Resolve visible providers registered by core or declared plugin dependencies |
| config:read | Read kernel configuration values via ConfigManager |
| events:emit | Emit typed kernel events |
| events:listen | Subscribe to kernel lifecycle or domain events |
| hooks:register | Attach handlers to kernel lifecycle hooks |
| health:register | Register readiness/liveness checks with HealthRegistry |

## SemVer compatibility, dependencies & conflicts

- forgeVersion ranges are checked against FORGE_CORE_VERSION using the built-in SemVer 2.0.0 engine before any plugin hook runs.
- Plugin dependencies are topologically sorted at boot and shut down in exact reverse order.
- Calling a PluginContext API outside declared capabilities throws PluginCapabilityError immediately.
- Conflicting plugins or circular plugin dependencies fail fast with PluginConflictError or CircularPluginDependencyError.

---

# Creating Plugins

> Author, validate, and test custom ForgeJS plugins with definePlugin(), Standard Schema config validation, and createPluginTestHarness().

- **Section**: Plugins & Extensions
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/testing
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/creating-plugins
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/creating-plugins.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Authoring with definePlugin()

Use definePlugin() with explicit capabilities, a forgeVersion SemVer range, and a Standard Schema v1 configSchema so invalid plugin configurations fail fast during the configure stage.

**File: `src/plugins/metrics.plugin.ts`**

```ts
import { createToken, definePlugin, FORGE_CORE_VERSION } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { z } from 'zod';

export interface MetricsClient {
  increment(metric: string): void;
}

export const MetricsToken = createToken<MetricsClient>('acme:metrics');

export const metricsPlugin = definePlugin({
  name: 'acme-metrics',
  version: '1.0.0',
  forgeVersion: `^${FORGE_CORE_VERSION}`,
  capabilities: ['di:register', 'health:register'],
  configSchema: z.object({
    namespace: z.string().min(1).default('app'),
  }),
  register(ctx, config) {
    ctx.registerProvider({
      token: MetricsToken,
      scope: 'singleton',
      useValue: {
        increment: (metric) => console.info(`[${config.namespace}] ${metric}`),
      },
    });
    ctx.registerHealthCheck('acme-metrics', () => ({ status: 'up' }));
  },
});
```

## Isolated plugin testing with createPluginTestHarness()

createPluginTestHarness({ plugin, config }) boots a real ApplicationKernel with your plugin, validates exported tokens via resolveExport(), checks health probes, and exercises teardown.

**File: `tests/metrics.plugin.test.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createToken, definePlugin } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createPluginTestHarness } from '@forge-fr/testing';
import { z } from 'zod';

const MetricsPortToken = createToken<number>('metrics.port');

const MetricsPlugin = definePlugin({
  name: 'metrics-plugin',
  version: '1.0.0',
  forgeVersion: '^1.0.0-rc.1',
  capabilities: ['di:register', 'health:register'],
  configSchema: z.object({ port: z.number().int().min(1024).default(9090) }),
  register(ctx, config) {
    ctx.registerProvider({ token: MetricsPortToken, useValue: config.port }, { export: true });
    ctx.registerHealthCheck('metrics', () => ({ status: 'ok' }));
  },
});

const harness = createPluginTestHarness({
  plugin: MetricsPlugin,
  config: { port: 9100 },
});

await harness.start();
assert.equal(harness.resolveExport(MetricsPortToken), 9100);
assert.equal((await harness.health()).status, 'ok');
await harness.shutdown();
```

# Adapter Development

> Implement custom HTTP runtime, database, cache, queue, or storage adapters and verify them against ForgeJS contract suites.

- **Section**: Plugins & Extensions
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/database, @forge-fr/testing

- **Updated**: 2026-11-26

- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/adapter-development.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## Shared adapter contract verification

Every official HTTP and WebSocket adapter passes the exact same behavioral contract suites exported by @forge-fr/testing: runHttpAdapterContractSuite() and runWebSocketContractSuite().

**File: `tests/custom-adapter.contract.test.ts`**

```ts
import { runHttpAdapterContractSuite } from '@forge-fr/testing';
import { createMyRuntimeAdapter } from '../src/my-adapter.js';

const report = await runHttpAdapterContractSuite({
  name: 'my-custom-runtime',
  createAdapter: () => createMyRuntimeAdapter(),
});

if (!report.passed) {
  throw new Error(`Adapter contract failed: ${JSON.stringify(report.results)}`);
}
```

## Building custom DatabaseAdapter drivers

- Implement connect(), disconnect(), ping(), transaction(fn, opts), and state transitions cleanly.
- Normalize driver-specific error codes into @forge-fr/database ForgeError subclasses with expose: false.
- Wrap your adapter with createDatabasePlugin() to automatically register DI tokens and health probes.

# Integrating External Libraries

> Use optional peerDependencies and duck-typed interfaces (RedisClientLike, PrismaClientLike) to keep core packages dependency-free.

- **Section**: Plugins & Extensions
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/cache, @forge-fr/prisma
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/external-libraries
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/plugins/external-libraries.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/PACKAGE_STRATEGY.md

## Duck-typed peer integration pattern

Packages like @forge-fr/cache, @forge-fr/queue, @forge-fr/prisma, and @forge-fr/auth accept narrow structural interfaces (RedisClientLike, PrismaClientLike, BetterAuthLike) so applications can upgrade peer clients cleanly without version-pin lock-in.

| Package | Structural Interface / Peer Strategy |
| --- | --- |
| @forge-fr/cache & @forge-fr/queue | RedisClientLike — works with ioredis or node-redis wrappers without hard runtime coupling |
| @forge-fr/prisma | PrismaClientLike — supports Prisma v5, v6, and v7+ generated clients |
| @forge-fr/validation | @standard-schema/spec v1 — Zod v4, Valibot v1, ArkType, plus zodAdapter for Zod v3 |
| @forge-fr/auth | Optional peer @node-rs/argon2 on Node.js; native Bun.password on Bun |

# Caching & Redis

> O(1) LRU memory cache, cursor SCAN-based Redis cache, single-flight getOrSet() stampede protection, and tag/prefix invalidation.

- **Section**: Advanced Features
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/cache
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/caching
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/caching.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/infrastructure-and-cli.md

## Single-flight caching & tag invalidation

getOrSet() coalesces concurrent cache misses for the same key into a single in-flight loader promise, preventing thundering-herd spikes against upstream databases.

**File: `src/cache.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createMemoryCacheAdapter } from '@forge-fr/cache';

const cache = createMemoryCacheAdapter({ maxEntries: 2_000 });
let loads = 0;

const [a, b] = await Promise.all([
  cache.getOrSet('profile:42', async () => {
    loads += 1;
    return { id: '42', tier: 'pro' };
  }, { ttlMs: 60_000, tags: ['user:42'] }),
  cache.getOrSet('profile:42', async () => {
    loads += 1;
    return { id: '42', tier: 'pro' };
  }, { ttlMs: 60_000, tags: ['user:42'] }),
]);

assert.equal(loads, 1);
assert.deepEqual(a, b);
await cache.invalidateTag('user:42');
```

## Non-blocking Redis SCAN invalidation

> **NOTE: Zero Blocking KEYS * Calls**
>
> createRedisCacheAdapter() uses incremental cursor SCAN batches for prefix and tag invalidation instead of blocking Redis KEYS * commands, and supports createCachePlugin() for kernel lifecycle wiring.

---

# Queues & Background Jobs

> Memory, Redis sorted-set (atomic Lua pop), and PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED job queues with retries, idempotency keys, DLQ replay, and graceful worker drain.

- **Section**: Advanced Features
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/queue
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/queues
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/queues.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/infrastructure-and-cli.md

## Enqueueing jobs & draining workers gracefully

@forge-fr/queue provides identical job semantics across createMemoryQueueAdapter(), createRedisQueueAdapter() (atomic Lua pop), and createPostgresQueueAdapter() (PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).

**File: `src/worker.ts`**

```ts
import { createMemoryQueueAdapter, createQueueWorker } from '@forge-fr/queue';

const queue = createMemoryQueueAdapter({ maxQueueSize: 1_000 });

const worker = createQueueWorker<{ invoiceId: string }>(
  queue,
  async (job, ctx) => {
    if (ctx.signal.aborted) return;
    console.info('Rendering PDF for', job.payload.invoiceId);
  },
  { pollIntervalMs: 25, concurrency: 4 },
);

worker.start();
await queue.enqueue(
  'invoice.pdf',
  { invoiceId: 'inv_99' },
  { idempotencyKey: 'inv_99', priority: 10 },
);

// On SIGTERM, wait for active jobs to finish cleanly:
await worker.stop({ timeoutMs: 5_000 });
```

## Retries, exponential backoff & Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)

- Failed jobs retry with bounded exponential backoff up to maxAttempts before moving to the Dead-Letter Queue.
- Inspect or replay dead-letter jobs programmatically via adapter.listDeadLetters() and adapter.replayDeadLetter(id).
- Note: ForgeJS ships durable job queues, not a built-in cron scheduler.

---

# Events & Hooks

> Typed EventDispatcher (fail-fast, collect, isolate error strategies) and priority HookRegistry pipelines in @forge-fr/core.

- **Section**: Advanced Features
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/events-and-hooks
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/events-and-hooks.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

## EventDispatcher error strategies

| Strategy | Behavior when a listener throws |
| --- | --- |
| fail-fast (default) | Stops dispatching immediately and rejects with the first listener error |
| collect | Runs all listeners and throws AggregateError if one or more fail |
| isolate | Runs all listeners and routes errors to onError without failing emit() |

**File: `src/events.ts`**

```ts
import { createEventDispatcher, createHookRegistry } from '@forge-fr/core';

type AppEvents = { 'user.created': { id: string; email: string } };
const events = createEventDispatcher<AppEvents>({ errorStrategy: 'collect' });

events.on('user.created', ({ id }) => {
  console.info('Audit user signup:', id);
});
await events.emit('user.created', { id: 'u_101', email: 'ada@example.com' });

const hooks = createHookRegistry<{ beforeSave: { entityId: string } }>();
hooks.add('beforeSave', (payload) => console.info('Saving', payload.entityId), { priority: 10 });
await hooks.run('beforeSave', { entityId: 'ord_55' });
```

# File Storage & S3

> Memory, symlink-jailed local disk, and zero-SDK Web Crypto AWS SigV4 S3 object storage with magic-byte upload validation.

- **Section**: Advanced Features
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/storage
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/storage
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/storage.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/infrastructure-and-cli.md

## Traversal-safe keys, symlink confinement & AWS SigV4

- All storage adapters normalize keys and reject path traversal (../, null bytes, absolute paths) with StoragePathError.
- createLocalStorageAdapter() jails writes inside the configured root using canonical realpath symlink verification.
- createS3StorageAdapter() signs AWS SigV4 requests via Web Crypto with zero AWS SDK dependencies and HTTPS enforced by default.
- verifyMagicBytesForMime() validates actual file binary headers against allowed MIME types.

**File: `src/storage.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {
  createMemoryStorageAdapter,
  StoragePathError,
  verifyMagicBytesForMime,
} from '@forge-fr/storage';

const storage = createMemoryStorageAdapter();
const pngHeader = new Uint8Array([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a]);

assert.equal(verifyMagicBytesForMime(pngHeader, 'image/png'), true);
await assert.rejects(
  () => storage.put('../etc/passwd', 'blocked', { contentType: 'text/plain' }),
  StoragePathError,
);

const stored = await storage.put('avatars/u1.png', pngHeader, { contentType: 'image/png' });
assert.equal(stored.key, 'avatars/u1.png');
```

# WebSockets & Server-Sent Events

> Cross-runtime app.ws() (RFC 6455 Node, native Bun.serve, Edge) with pre-upgrade auth, CSWSH allowedOrigins, and createSseResponse() streaming.

- **Section**: Advanced Features
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, @forge-fr/edge
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/realtime
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/realtime.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/http-and-validation.md

## Pre-upgrade WebSocket security & SSE streaming

app.ws(path, handlers, options) validates Origin allowlists (preventing Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking) and executes authenticate(ctx) before sending 101 Switching Protocols.

**File: `src/realtime.ts`**

```ts
import { createHttpApp, createSseResponse } from '@forge-fr/http';

const app = createHttpApp();

app.ws(
  '/ws/chat/:room',
  {
    authenticate(ctx) {
      return ctx.headers.get('authorization') === 'Bearer secret';
    },
    onOpen(ws) {
      ws.send(`joined:${ws.params['room']}`);
    },
    onMessage(ws, message) {
      ws.send(`echo:${String(message)}`);
    },
  },
  {
    allowedOrigins: ['https://app.example.com'],
    maxPayloadBytes: 64 * 1024,
  },
);

app.get('/events', () =>
  createSseResponse(async (stream) => {
    await stream.send({ event: 'ready', data: { ok: true } });
    stream.close();
  }),
);
```

# Logging, Metrics, Tracing & Health Checks

> Structured Pino logging with secret & URL redaction, CRLF neutralization, correlation IDs, OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics, and sanitized /health/live & /health/ready endpoints.

- **Section**: Advanced Features
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/logger
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/observability
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/advanced/observability.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/security-and-observability.md

## Redacted Pino logging, correlation IDs & health probes

@forge-fr/logger automatically redacts SecretValue objects, password/token keys, and credentialed database URLs, strips CRLF log-injection newlines, propagates x-correlation-id headers, and serves production-safe health endpoints.

**File: `src/observability.ts`**

```ts
import { secret } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import {
  createCorrelationIdMiddleware,
  createMemoryLogSink,
  createPinoLogger,
  registerHealthRoutes,
} from '@forge-fr/logger';

const sink = createMemoryLogSink();
const logger = createPinoLogger({ destination: sink.stream });

logger.info('db.connect', {
  databaseUrl: 'postgres://user:secretpass@db.local:5432/app',
  apiKey: secret('sk_live_very_secret_value'),
});

const app = createHttpApp();
app.use(createCorrelationIdMiddleware());
registerHealthRoutes(app, { registry: app.kernel.health });
```

## OpenTelemetry tracing & metrics

Mount createObservabilityPlugin() or createTelemetryMiddleware() to connect @opentelemetry/api tracer spans and HTTP latency histograms without hard-coupling your domain layer to a specific APM vendor.

# Testing

> In-memory HTTP/WebSocket tests, DI provider overrides, plugin harnesses, and dual-runtime Node.js + Bun verification.

- **Section**: Testing & Production
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/testing
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/testing
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/testing.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/TESTING_STRATEGY.md

## Fast in-memory HTTP, DI & WebSocket testing

- createTestClient(app) exercises full routing, tiered middleware, hooks, body limits, and schema validation without binding TCP sockets.
- overrideProvider() swaps repositories or external services cleanly inside the DI container.
- createMemoryWebSocketPair() tests real-time WebSocket upgrades, auth guards, and message frames deterministically.
- createPluginTestHarness() verifies plugin configuration schemas, exports, health probes, and shutdown hooks in isolation.

**File: `tests/orders.test.ts`**

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createKernel, createToken } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createTestClient, overrideProvider } from '@forge-fr/testing';

const TaxRateToken = createToken<number>('TaxRate');
const kernel = createKernel({
  providers: [{ token: TaxRateToken, scope: 'singleton', useValue: 0.2 }],
});

overrideProvider(kernel.container, TaxRateToken, 0.1);
await kernel.start();

const app = createHttpApp({ kernel });
app.get('/tax', (ctx) => ctx.json({ rate: ctx.container!.resolve(TaxRateToken) }));

const client = createTestClient(app);
const res = await client.get('/tax');
assert.deepEqual(await res.json(), { rate: 0.1 });
await client.close();
```

# Runtime Compatibility

> Transparent compatibility matrix separating locally verified runtimes (Node.js v22.23.5, Bun 1.4.4) from CI-configured targets.

- **Section**: Testing & Production
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, @forge-fr/edge
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/runtime-compatibility
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/runtime-compatibility.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/RUNTIME_COMPATIBILITY.md

## Verified & configured runtime matrix

| Runtime | Declared Target | Local Verification | CI Matrix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js 22 LTS | >= 22.18.0 | Verified locally (v22.23.5 — 21/21 smoke) | ubuntu · macos · windows |
| Bun 1.4+ | >= 1.4.0 | Verified locally (1.4.4 — 23/23 smoke) | ubuntu · macos (1.4.4) |
| WinterCG Edge | Web Fetch API | Unit & contract verified (no local workerd/deno binary) | Included in Node & Bun jobs |
| Node.js 24 LTS | >= 22.18.0 | Not installed locally | ubuntu-latest (Node 24) |
| PostgreSQL 16 | postgres-js / Drizzle / Prisma | Skipped locally (no Docker daemon) | postgres:16-alpine service job |

## Cloudflare Workers & Deno Deploy (@forge-fr/edge)

**File: `src/edge.ts`**

```ts
import { createCloudflareWorkerHandler, createDenoHandler, getEdgeEnv } from '@forge-fr/edge';
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.get('/region', (ctx) => {
  const env = getEdgeEnv<{ readonly REGION: string }>(ctx.request);
  return ctx.json({ runtime: ctx.runtime, region: env?.REGION ?? 'local' });
});

export default createCloudflareWorkerHandler<{ readonly REGION: string }>(app, {
  trustCfConnectingIp: true,
});
export const denoHandler = createDenoHandler(app);
```

# Production Deployment

> Strict ESM builds, NODE_ENV=production hardening, POSIX graceful draining, health probes, and reverse-proxy configuration.

- **Section**: Testing & Production
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun, @forge-fr/edge, @forge-fr/logger
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/production
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/production.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md

## Production deployment checklist

- Run with NODE_ENV=production and exposeErrorDetails: false so unknown 5xx errors and readiness probes sanitize internal diagnostics.
- Attach attachProcessShutdown(server, { timeoutMs: 10_000 }) alongside kernel.shutdown() for zero-drop SIGTERM/SIGINT draining.
- Keep trustProxy: false unless behind a trusted reverse proxy (Nginx, Caddy, Envoy, Cloudflare) that overwrites client IP headers.
- Mount /health/live (liveness) and /health/ready (readiness) via registerHealthRoutes() for container orchestrator probes.

## Node.js & Bun production entrypoint

**Node.js (`src/index.ts`)**

```ts
import { createNodeAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/node';
import { app, kernel } from './app.js';

await kernel.start();
const server = createNodeAdapter(app);
await server.listen({ host: '0.0.0.0', port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000) });

attachProcessShutdown(server, {
  timeoutMs: 10_000,
  onAfterStop: async () => {
    await kernel.shutdown();
  },
});
```

**Bun (`src/index.ts`)**

```ts
import { createBunAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/bun';
import { app, kernel } from './app.js';

await kernel.start();
const server = createBunAdapter(app);
await server.listen({ host: '0.0.0.0', port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000) });

attachProcessShutdown(server, {
  timeoutMs: 10_000,
  onAfterStop: async () => {
    await kernel.shutdown();
  },
});
```

# Performance & Benchmarks

> Hot-path HTTP optimizations and verbatim reproducible Node.js v22.23.5 & Bun 1.4.4 benchmark results from benchmarks/RESULTS.md.

- **Section**: Testing & Production
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/router, @forge-fr/http, @forge-fr/node, @forge-fr/bun
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/performance
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/deployment/performance.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/benchmarks/RESULTS.md

## Hot-path engineering

- Pre-normalization O(1) staticByMethod lookup and reused scratch-array radix matching in @forge-fr/router.
- Compact 13-field ForgeContext with lazy on-demand requestId and inline route._pipelineRun caching in @forge-fr/http.
- Direct-meta FastNodeRequest & FastResponse on Node.js; pure-HTTP Bun.serve mode with pre-allocated Headers presets on Bun.
- compileFastValidator() direct Zod v4 safeParse fast path with automatic Standard Schema fallback.

## Measured results (Node.js v22.23.5 & Bun 1.4.4)

Measured on Linux 4.19.0-gvisor (x64, 2 vCPU, 4096 MB RAM) comparing ForgeJS against Hono ^4.13.22 and Fastify ^5.12.8 across identical 24-route tables (concurrency = 24, warmup = 600ms, duration = 1200ms).

| Benchmark Scenario | ForgeJS | Hono | Fastify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node 22 — In-Process Static JSON (ops/s) | 317,446 | 131,194 | 15,197 |
| Node 22 — In-Process 5-Middleware (ops/s) | 254,577 | 97,585 | 22,392 |
| Node 22 — Live HTTP Static JSON (req/s) | 3,867.36 | 3,724.83 | 3,864.97 |
| Node 22 — Live HTTP 5-Middleware (req/s) | 3,977.83 | 3,755.81 | 3,898.31 |
| Node 22 — Live HTTP Zod POST (req/s) | 3,336.7 | 3,062.38 | 3,435.71 |
| Bun 1.4 — In-Process Static JSON (ops/s) | 721,724 | 525,907 | 44,613 |
| Bun 1.4 — Live HTTP 5-Middleware (req/s) | 8,216.07 | 7,005.5 | 6,796.26 |
| Bun 1.4 — Live HTTP Static JSON (req/s) | 7,275.57 | 7,570.29 | 6,538.15 |
| Cold Start Median — Node 22 / Bun 1.4 (ms) | 61.01 / 11.08 | 61.44 / 10.79 | 163.92 / 112.25 |

## Reproduce identically

**File: `terminal`**

```bash
node benchmarks/run-all.mjs
bun benchmarks/run-all.mjs
```

# CLI Reference (@forge-fr/cli)

> Complete reference for all 10 verified forge CLI commands, flags, templates, expected output, and error codes from packages/cli/src/commands.ts.

- **Section**: CLI Reference
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/cli
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/cli/reference
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/cli/reference.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/docs/infrastructure-and-cli.md

## All 10 verified commands

@forge-fr/cli ships the cross-runtime forge binary (Node.js >=22.18 and Bun >=1.4) with zero third-party runtime dependencies, shell: false process execution, and prototype-safe package.json editing.

| Command | Usage | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| forge new | forge new <name> [--template minimal\|api\|modular] [--runtime node\|bun\|edge] | Scaffold a strict-ESM TypeScript ForgeJS application with runtime adapter setup. |
| forge generate | forge generate\|g <module\|controller\|service> <name> | Generate typed module, controller, or service boilerplate following layered boundaries. |
| forge plugin add | forge plugin add <plugin> | Register an official @forge-fr/* plugin into your project configuration safely. |
| forge dev | forge dev [--watch] [--runtime node\|bun] | Start the development server on Node.js or Bun with optional file watch mode. |
| forge build | forge build | Compile TypeScript sources into production ESM artifacts. |
| forge start | forge start | Launch the compiled production application entrypoint. |
| forge test | forge test | Run the project test suite via the configured test runner. |
| forge doctor | forge doctor [--json] | Inspect runtime versions, TypeScript configuration, ESM mode, and workspace health. |
| forge help | forge help | Display CLI usage instructions and available flags. |
| forge version | forge version | Print the installed @forge-fr/cli version. |

## Command options & error codes

| Command | Supported Options / Flags | Error Codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| forge new <name> | --template <api\|modular>, --runtime <auto\|node\|bun\|edge>, --port <1..65535>, --dir <path>, --dry-run, --force | CLI_INVALID_ARGUMENT, CLI_FILE_EXISTS |
| forge generate <type> <name> | type: module \| controller \| service (alias: g); --dir <path>, --dry-run, --force | CLI_INVALID_ARGUMENT, CLI_FILE_EXISTS |
| forge plugin add <plugin> | --dir <path>, --dry-run (sanitizes & sorts package.json dependencies) | CLI_INVALID_ARGUMENT, CLI_EXECUTION_FAILED |
| forge dev / build / start / test | --runtime <auto\|node\|bun>, --watch (dev), --dir <path> | CLI_INVALID_ARGUMENT |
| forge doctor | --json (machine-readable DoctorReport), --dir <path> | Exits 1 if Node.js < 22 |

## Common CLI workflows & expected output

**File: `terminal`**

```bash
# 1. Scaffold a modular backend
npx @forge-fr/cli@next new payments-api --template modular --runtime node
# => Created ForgeJS project "payments-api" at ./payments-api

# 2. Generate typed feature artifacts (alias: forge g)
forge generate module webhooks
forge generate controller webhooks
forge generate service webhooks

# 3. Register an official plugin & inspect workspace health
forge plugin add security
forge doctor --json
```

# Contributing

> Monorepo workspace layout, strict TypeScript standards, architectural boundary tests, and verification commands for contributors.

- **Section**: Community & Contributing

## Repository standards & boundary rules

- Strict TypeScript: strict: true, exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true, pure ESM only.
- Zero node:* or Bun globals in core, router, http, validation, openapi, authorization, security, or edge packages.
- All 20 packages share synchronized versions and must remain acyclic in the workspace dependency graph.

npx vitest run

# Plugin Author Guide

> Checklist for publishing pure-ESM, capability-scoped third-party ForgeJS plugins with SemVer safety and clean npm pack tarballs.

- **Section**: Community & Contributing
- **Packages**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/testing
- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/community/plugin-author-guide
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/community/plugin-author-guide.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/PACKAGE_STRATEGY.md

## Publication & hygiene checklist

- Declare minimum required capabilities in definePlugin() and validate config with Standard Schema v1.
- Ship pure ESM with strict exports map ("exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" } }).
- Declare heavy client libraries (e.g., ioredis, @prisma/client) as optional peerDependencies using narrow duck-typed interfaces.
- Verify lifecycle, health probes, and teardown via createPluginTestHarness() and inspect npm pack --dry-run before publishing.

## Reference package.json exports map

**File: `package.json`**

```json
{
  "name": "forgejs-plugin-example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/index.js"
    }
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@forge-fr/core": "^1.0.0-rc.1"
  }
}
```

- **Updated**: 2026-11-26
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/community/faq
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/docs/community/faq.md
- **Source**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/blob/main/FRAMEWORK_FEATURE_INVENTORY.md

## Why does ForgeJS use typed tokens instead of decorators?

Explicit createToken<T>() and defineModule() avoid experimental decorator metadata overhead, preserve strict TypeScript inference without reflection polyfills, and keep cold starts fast across Node.js, Bun, and Edge.

## Which ORMs and databases are officially supported?

ForgeJS provides official packages for native PostgreSQL (@forge-fr/database via postgres-js), Drizzle ORM (@forge-fr/drizzle), and Prisma ORM (@forge-fr/prisma). TypeORM, MikroORM, Sequelize, and Knex are not shipped officially, though teams can integrate them via DatabaseAdapter.

## Is v1.0.0-rc.1 published on npm yet?

All 20 packages are verified locally via npm pack tarballs and isolated Node 22 & Bun 1.4 consumer tests, with .github/workflows/release.yml configured for OIDC Trusted Publishing. Live registry publication awaits maintainer dispatch.

## Does ForgeJS guarantee my application is secure out of the box?

No framework can guarantee application security alone. ForgeJS enforces hardened HTTP defaults (bounded bodies, prototype sanitization, redacted errors) and ships OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 primitives, while your team remains responsible for calling ownership/tenant checks, TLS termination, secret management, and WAF/DDoS infrastructure.

---

# @forge-fr/core

> 7-stage application kernel, typed dependency injection container, encapsulated modules, SemVer capability-scoped plugin runtime, errors, secrets, config, events, hooks, and health checks.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Framework Core
- **Category**: core
- **Tarball**: 50.5 kB (56 files)
- **Internal deps**: none
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/core
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/core.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/core
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Zero third-party runtime dependencies and zero node:* or Bun globals. Runs identically on Node.js >=22.18.0, Bun >=1.4.0, and WinterCG Edge.
- **Errors**: All framework errors inherit from ForgeError. Production serialization strips details when expose is false (default for 5xx errors).

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createKernel, createToken, defineModule, secret } from '@forge-fr/core';

const ApiKeyToken = createToken<string>('ApiKey');

const ConfigModule = defineModule({
  name: 'app-config',
  providers: [
    { token: ApiKeyToken, scope: 'singleton', useValue: secret(process.env.API_KEY ?? 'dev').reveal() },
  ],
  exports: [ApiKeyToken],
});

const kernel = createKernel({ modules: [ConfigModule] });
await kernel.start();
```

## Public Exports

### Application Kernel

- **Values**: `createKernel`, `KernelConfigToken`, `KernelEventsToken`, `KernelLoggerToken`, `LifecycleError`
- **Types**: `AnyForgePlugin`, `ApplicationKernel`, `KernelEventMap`, `KernelHookContext`, `KernelHooks`, `KernelOptions`, `KernelPluginInput`, `KernelState`, `LifecycleErrorEvent`, `LifecycleStage`, `LifecycleStageEvent`

### Dependency Injection

- **Values**: `createContainer`, `createToken`, `isToken`, `CircularDependencyError`, `ContainerDisposedError`, `ProviderNotFoundError`, `ScopeViolationError`
- **Types**: `AliasProvider`, `ClassProvider`, `Container`, `DependencyResolver`, `Disposer`, `FactoryProvider`, `InjectableConstructor`, `InjectionToken`, `ProviderDefinition`, `ProviderScope`, `RegisterOptions`, `ValueProvider`

### Modules

- **Values**: `defineModule`, `createModuleRegistry`, `CircularModuleDependencyError`, `ModuleConfigurationError`, `ProviderNotVisibleError`
- **Types**: `AnyProviderDefinition`, `ForgeModule`, `ModuleConfigureContext`, `ModuleDefinition`, `ModuleLifecycleContext`, `ModuleRegistry`, `ModuleRegistryOptions`

### Plugins & SemVer

- **Values**: `FORGE_CORE_VERSION`, `definePlugin`, `createPluginRegistry`, `createPluginContext`, `validatePluginConfig`, `parseSemVer`, `isValidSemVer`, `compareSemVer`, `isValidSemVerRange`, `satisfiesRange`, `CircularPluginDependencyError`, `PluginCapabilityError`, `PluginCompatibilityError`, `PluginConfigError`, `PluginConflictError`, `PluginDefinitionError`, `PluginDependencyError`, `PluginEncapsulationError`, `PluginLifecycleError`
- **Types**: `ForgePlugin`, `ForgePluginDefinition`, `PluginCapability`, `PluginConfigIssue`, `PluginContext`, `PluginContextRuntimeBridge`, `PluginDependencySpec`, `PluginHookEvent`, `PluginHookStage`, `PluginProviderRegisterOptions`, `PluginRegistry`, `PluginRegistryOptions`, `RegisteredPlugin`, `ResolvedPluginEntry`, `SemVer`, `StandardSchemaIssueLike`, `StandardSchemaLike`

- **Types**: `ForgeErrorOptions`, `PublicErrorBody`, `PublicErrorSerializationOptions`, `SecretValue`

# @forge-fr/router

> Zero-dependency radix router with O(1) static route lookup, constrained parameters, wildcard matching, nested groups, automatic HEAD, and RFC 405 Allow generation.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Framework Core
- **Category**: core
- **Tarball**: 16.4 kB (24 files)
- **Internal deps**: none
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/router
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/router.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/router
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Zero runtime dependencies. Pure ESM radix tree with O(1) static route lookup and reused scratch arrays.
- **Errors**: Throws RouterError on duplicate static routes, invalid parameter names (including prototype keys), or malformed constraints.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createRouter } from '@forge-fr/router';

const router = createRouter();
router.get('/users/:id{\\d+}', { name: 'getUser' });

const matched = router.match('GET', '/users/42');
// matched.status === 'found', matched.params.id === '42'
```

## Public Exports

### Router Engine

- **Values**: `createRouter`, `HTTP_METHODS`, `RouterError`
- **Types**: `GroupOptions`, `HttpMethod`, `ParamConstraint`, `RegisteredRoute`, `RouteBuilder`, `RouteMatchResult`, `RouteOptions`, `Router`, `RouterErrorCode`, `RouterOptions`

# @forge-fr/http

> Web Standards HTTP engine with tiered middleware, 7 lifecycle hooks, bounded body parsers, SSE, Web Streams compression, conditional ETags, and WebSocket route registry.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Framework Core
- **Category**: core
- **Tarball**: 52.5 kB (56 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/router
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/http
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/http.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/http
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Built on Web Standards (Request, Response, Headers, ReadableStream, CompressionStream). Zero third-party dependencies.
- **Errors**: Enforces 1 MiB default body limit (PayloadTooLargeError 413), CR/LF/NUL rejection in FastHeaders, and double-next() / post-commit middleware guards.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createHttpApp, createCompressionMiddleware, createEtagMiddleware } from '@forge-fr/http';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.use(createCompressionMiddleware());
app.use(createEtagMiddleware());

app.get('/ping', (ctx) => ctx.json({ pong: true }));
```

## Public Exports

### Application & Middleware

- **Values**: `createHttpApp`, `composeMiddleware`, `sortMiddleware`, `createCompressionMiddleware`, `createEtagMiddleware`
- **Types**: `ForgeHttpApp`, `ForgeContext`, `ForgeMiddleware`, `ForgeRouteHandler`, `HttpAppOptions`, `HttpGroupOptions`, `HttpMethod`, `HttpRouteOptions`, `HttpRuntimeAdapter`, `ListenOptions`, `MiddlewareNext`, `MiddlewareRegistrationOptions`, `MiddlewareTier`, `RegisteredMiddleware`, `RegisteredRoute`, `ResponseHelperInit`, `RouteHandlerResult`, `ServerAddress`, `CompressionOptions`, `SupportedCompressionEncoding`, `EtagOptions`, `FetchHandler`, `RedirectStatusCode`, `RuntimeRequestMeta`

- **Types**: `BodyParseOptions`, `ParsedMultipart`, `UploadedFile`, `RequestBodyReader`, `AcceptMediaRange`, `CreateSseResponseOptions`, `SseEvent`, `SseProducer`, `SseStreamController`

# @forge-fr/node

> Native node:http runtime adapter with direct-dispatch request metadata, synchronous FastResponse writes, RFC 6455 WebSocket upgrade codec, and POSIX graceful shutdown.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: runtime
- **Tarball**: 22.6 kB (20 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/http
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/node
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/node.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/node
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Requires Node.js >=22.18.0 (verified locally on v22.23.5). Uses native node:http and zero-dep RFC 6455 WebSockets.
- **Errors**: Propagates client disconnects via AbortSignal and drains active connections cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM via attachProcessShutdown.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createNodeAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/node';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true }));

const server = await app.listen(createNodeAdapter(), { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3000 });
attachProcessShutdown(server);
```

## Public Exports

### Node.js Runtime Adapter & Shutdown

- **Values**: `NodeAdapter`, `createNodeAdapter`, `attachProcessShutdown`
- **Types**: `NodeAdapterOptions`, `ProcessLike`, `ProcessShutdownHandle`, `ProcessShutdownOptions`, `ProcessShutdownTarget`, `ShutdownSignal`

---

# @forge-fr/bun

> Native Bun.serve() runtime adapter with pure-HTTP fast mode, native Bun WebSockets, in-flight request draining, and POSIX shutdown handling.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: runtime
- **Tarball**: 11.9 kB (16 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/http
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/bun
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/bun.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/bun
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Requires Bun >=1.4.0 (verified locally on Bun 1.4.4). Automatically selects pure-HTTP mode when no WebSocket routes exist.
- **Errors**: Enforces maxRequestBodySize and clamped idleTimeout while draining active integer inFlightCount during shutdown.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createBunAdapter, attachProcessShutdown } from '@forge-fr/bun';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.get('/health', (ctx) => ctx.json({ ok: true }));

const server = await app.listen(createBunAdapter(), { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3000 });
attachProcessShutdown(server);
```

# @forge-fr/edge

> WinterCG Fetch adapter for Cloudflare Workers, Deno, and isolate runtimes with zero node:* or Bun globals and waitUntil background task helpers.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: runtime
- **Tarball**: 8.8 kB (12 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/http
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/edge
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/edge.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/edge
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Zero node:* or Bun globals. Unit and Fetch/WebSocketPair contract verified; live workerd/deno binaries are not installed in local sandbox.
- **Errors**: Background promises submitted via runInEdgeBackground() use executionCtx.waitUntil when available.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { createCloudflareWorkerHandler, getEdgeEnv } from '@forge-fr/edge';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.get('/env', (ctx) => ctx.json({ hasEnv: Boolean(getEdgeEnv(ctx.request)) }));

export default createCloudflareWorkerHandler(app);
```

# @forge-fr/validation

> Standard Schema v1 validation engine with Zod v4 direct fast path, typed route handler wrapper, response schema stripping, and recursive prototype-pollution sanitization.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: validation
- **Tarball**: 13.6 kB (24 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http
- **Runtime deps**: @standard-schema/spec ^1.1.0
- **Peer deps**: zod >=3.24 || >=4 (optional), valibot >=1 (optional)
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/validation
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/validation.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/validation
```

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Built on @standard-schema/spec v1 with a direct Zod v4 safeParse fast path and automatic Standard Schema fallback.
- **Errors**: Invalid request inputs throw ValidationError (400). Invalid outgoing responses throw ResponseValidationError (500, expose: false) to prevent accidental PII leakage.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createHttpApp } from '@forge-fr/http';
import { validatedHandler } from '@forge-fr/validation';
import { z } from 'zod';

const app = createHttpApp();
app.post(
  '/items',
  validatedHandler(
    {
      body: z.object({ name: z.string().min(2) }),
      response: z.object({ ok: z.literal(true), name: z.string() }),
    },
    (ctx, input) => ctx.json({ ok: true, name: input.body.name }),
  ),
);
```

## Public Exports

### Validation Engine & Schema Adapters

- **Values**: `validate`, `validateOrThrow`, `createSchemaValidator`, `formatStandardIssues`, `isStandardSchema`, `ResponseValidationError`, `zodAdapter`, `valibotAdapter`, `customSchema`, `fromStandardSchema`
- **Types**: `AnySchema`, `CustomValidateFn`, `InferInput`, `InferOutput`, `LegacySafeParseIssue`, `LegacyZodLikeSchema`, `SchemaValidator`, `StandardSchemaV1`, `ValidateOptions`, `ValidationFailure`, `ValidationIssue`, `ValidationResult`, `ValidationSuccess`

### HTTP Validation Helpers

- **Values**: `validatedHandler`, `validateRequest`, `getValidated`, `VALIDATED_STATE_KEY`
- **Types**: `HttpValidationOptions`, `RouteValidationSchemas`, `ValidatedInput`, `ValidatedRouteHandler`, `ValidationTarget`

# @forge-fr/database

> Native PostgreSQL adapter built on postgres-js with SQLSTATE error normalization, credential-redacted URLs, allowlisted transaction isolation, and checksum-verified migrations.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: database
- **Tarball**: 17.9 kB (28 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/core
- **Runtime deps**: postgres ^3.4.0 || ^4.0.0
- **Peer deps**: none
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/database
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/database.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/database
```

## Plugin Metadata

- **Factory**: `createPostgresPlugin / createDatabasePlugin`
- **Tokens**: `DefaultDatabaseTokens`
- **Health probe**: `database`
- **Capabilities**: `di:register`, `health:register`

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Built on postgres (postgres-js). Live PostgreSQL 16 integration tests run in CI when FORGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL is configured.
- **Errors**: Normalizes SQLSTATE codes (23505, 23503, 23502, 23514, 40001) into typed DatabaseError subclasses with expose: false by default.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createKernel, secret } from '@forge-fr/core';
import { createPostgresPlugin, DefaultDatabaseTokens } from '@forge-fr/database';

const kernel = createKernel({
  plugins: [[createPostgresPlugin(), { url: secret(process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? '') }]],
});
await kernel.start();
const adapter = kernel.container.resolve(DefaultDatabaseTokens.adapter);
```

## Public Exports

### PostgreSQL Adapter, Plugins & Migrations

- **Values**: `createDatabasePlugin`, `createPostgresAdapter`, `createPostgresPlugin`, `postgresConfigSchema`, `DefaultDatabaseTokens`, `createDatabaseToken`, `runInTransaction`, `createMigrationCoordinator`
- **Types**: `DatabaseAdapter`, `DatabaseConnectionState`, `DatabasePingResult`, `DatabasePluginOptions`, `DatabaseTokens`, `Migration`, `MigrationCoordinator`, `MigrationCoordinatorOptions`, `MigrationHooks`, `MigrationRecord`, `MigrationRunResult`, `MigrationStateStore`, `PostgresAdapterOptions`, `PostgresClientLike`, `PostgresDriverFactory`, `PostgresPluginOptions`, `PostgresSslMode`, `TransactionIsolationLevel`, `TransactionOptions`

### Database Errors & URL Redaction

- **Values**: `DatabaseError`, `DatabaseConnectionError`, `DatabaseUniqueViolationError`, `DatabaseForeignKeyViolationError`, `DatabaseNotNullViolationError`, `DatabaseCheckViolationError`, `DatabaseSerializationError`, `DatabaseTimeoutError`, `normalizeDatabaseError`, `redactDatabaseUrl`, `MigrationChecksumError`, `MigrationRollbackError`
- **Types**: `DatabaseErrorOptions`

# @forge-fr/drizzle

> First-class Drizzle ORM plugin preserving native PostgresJsDatabase<TSchema> inference, typed transactions, and DrizzleQueryError SQLSTATE normalization.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: database
- **Tarball**: 8.6 kB (16 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/database
- **Runtime deps**: zero runtime dependencies
- **Peer deps**: drizzle-orm >=0.40.0 <1.0.0
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/drizzle
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/drizzle.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/drizzle
```

## Plugin Metadata

- **Factory**: `createDrizzlePostgresPlugin`
- **Tokens**: `DefaultDrizzleTokens`
- **Health probe**: `drizzle`
- **Capabilities**: `di:register`, `health:register`

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Zero third-party runtime dependencies; peer depends on drizzle-orm >=0.40.0 <1.0.0. Preserves 100% native PostgresJsDatabase<TSchema> inference.
- **Errors**: normalizeDrizzleError unwraps DrizzleQueryError causes so SQLSTATE violations map cleanly to ForgeJS DatabaseError classes.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createDrizzlePostgresPlugin, DefaultDrizzleTokens } from '@forge-fr/drizzle';
import { createKernel, secret } from '@forge-fr/core';
import * as schema from './schema.js';

const kernel = createKernel({
  plugins: [
    [createDrizzlePostgresPlugin<typeof schema>(), { url: secret(process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? ''), schema }],
  ],
});
await kernel.start();
const db = kernel.container.resolve(DefaultDrizzleTokens.db);
```

## Public Exports

### Drizzle ORM Adapter & Plugin

- **Values**: `DefaultDrizzleTokens`, `createDrizzleToken`, `createDrizzleAdapter`, `createDrizzlePostgresAdapter`, `createDrizzlePostgresPlugin`, `drizzlePostgresConfigSchema`, `normalizeDrizzleError`
- **Types**: `DrizzleCasing`, `DrizzlePostgresAdapter`, `DrizzlePostgresClient`, `DrizzlePostgresConfig`, `DrizzlePostgresPluginOptions`, `DrizzlePostgresTx`, `DrizzleTokens`, `GenericDrizzleAdapterOptions`, `InferDrizzleTx`

## Runtime & Error Semantics

# @forge-fr/auth

> OWASP Argon2id password hashing (Node & Bun cross-compatible), algorithm-pinned JWT/JWKS, SHA-256 hashed sessions & API keys, OAuth 2.0 PKCE/OIDC, and Better Auth bridge.

- **Version**: v1.0.0-rc.1
- **Layer**: Adapter Layer
- **Category**: security
- **Tarball**: 27.6 kB (48 files)
- **Internal deps**: @forge-fr/core, @forge-fr/http
- **Runtime deps**: jose ^6.2.18
- **Peer deps**: @node-rs/argon2 >=2.0.0 (optional), better-auth >=1.0.0 (optional)
- **HTML URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/auth
- **Markdown URL**: https://github.com/forge-fr/forgejs/api/auth.md

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forge-fr/auth
```

## Plugin Metadata

- **Factory**: `createAuthPlugin`
- **Tokens**: `AuthTokens`
- **Health probe**: `auth`
- **Capabilities**: `di:register`, `health:register`

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Uses jose for JWT/JWKS. Argon2id password hashing is verified cross-compatible between @node-rs/argon2 (Node.js) and native Bun.password (Bun).
- **Errors**: Blocks alg: none, requires explicit JWT algorithms allowlist and >=32-byte HMAC secrets, hashes session IDs and API keys with SHA-256 before persistence.

## Usage Example

```ts
import { createArgon2PasswordHasher, createJwtService } from '@forge-fr/auth';

const hasher = createArgon2PasswordHasher();
const hash = await hasher.hash('correct-horse-battery-staple');
const valid = await hasher.verify('correct-horse-battery-staple', hash);
```

- **Tokens**: `SecurityTokens`
- **Health probe**: `security`
- **Capabilities**: `di:register`, `health:register`

## Runtime & Error Semantics

- **Runtime**: Zero third-party runtime dependencies. Aligns with OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 controls across headers, CORS, CSRF, rate limits, and SSRF.
